title: Safety and immunogenicity of an mRNA COVID-19 vaccine administered to adults: A phase 2, randomized, active-controlled trial.
abstract: We conducted a phase 2, randomized, active-controlled, observer-blind study (NCT05960097) among healthy adults ≥18 y of age who completed a primary COVID-19 mRNA vaccination series, with or without a booster, ≥3 months earlier. Participants were randomized (1:1:1:1:1) to either receive an investigational bivalent mRNA COVID-19 vaccine encoding ancestral D614G and Omicron BA.4-5 spike proteins (CV0701 mRNA vaccine) at one of three dose levels, an investigational monovalent mRNA COVID-19 vaccine encoding the Omicron BA.4-5 spike protein (CV0601 mRNA vaccine), or a licensed Original Wuhan/Omicron BA.4-5 bivalent mRNA COVID-19 vaccine. The primary objectives were to evaluate reactogenicity, safety and immunogenicity post-vaccination. Secondary and tertiary objectives were to further evaluate humoral and cell-mediated immunity post-vaccination. In total, 425 participants were vaccinated and 381 were included in the Day 29 per-protocol immunogenicity analysis. Most solicited events were mild to moderate. No vaccine-related serious adverse events or myocarditis/pericarditis cases were reported. For the CV0701 mRNA vaccine, a dose-dependent increase in Day 29 neutralizing titers against ancestral D614G and Omicron BA.4-5 was observed. Neutralizing titers against ancestral D614G and Omicron BA.4-5 declined by Days 91 and 181, but remained above baseline. Similar immune responses were observed for the CV0601 mRNA vaccine. At Day 8, CD4+ T cells (Th1 profile) increased in all study groups and CD8+ T cells increased in all study groups, except the lowest CV0701 dose group. The CV0701 and CV0601 mRNA vaccines elicited robust humoral and cellular immunity with an acceptable safety profile, comparable to a licensed, bivalent mRNA vaccine. Clinical Trial Registration EU CT number: 2023-504596-25-00 ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT05960097.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate the safety and immunogenicity of an mRNA COVID-19 vaccine in adults who had previously completed a primary vaccination series with or without a booster, addressing the need for improved vaccine strategies against emerging variants.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A phase 2, randomized, active-controlled trial was conducted among healthy adults aged ≥18 years who had completed a primary COVID-19 mRNA vaccination series, with or without a booster, at least 3 months prior.
analysis.methods: Participants were randomized in a 1:1:1:1:1 ratio to receive either an investigational bivalent mRNA vaccine encoding ancestral D614G and Omicron BA.4-5 spike proteins, an investigational monovalent mRNA vaccine encoding Omicron BA.4-5 spike protein, or a licensed Original Wuhan/Omicron BA.4-5 bivalent mRNA vaccine.
analysis.main_results: At Day 8, CD4+ T cells (Th1 profile) increased in all study groups, while CD8+ T cells increased in all groups except the lowest CV0701 dose group. No vaccine-related serious adverse events or myocarditis/pericarditis cases were reported.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study demonstrated that the investigational vaccines elicited robust humoral and cellular immunity with an acceptable safety profile, comparable to a licensed bivalent mRNA vaccine.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide cautious support for the use of these investigational vaccines in boosting immunity against SARS-CoV-2 variants, particularly in adults with prior vaccination histories.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited to healthy adults and did not include long-term follow-up, but the evidence is strong due to the randomized, controlled design and the inclusion of multiple vaccine types.

analysis.summary_en: This phase 2, randomized, active-controlled trial evaluated the safety and immunogenicity of two investigational mRNA vaccines (CV0701 and CV0601) encoding SARS-CoV-2 spike proteins, compared to a licensed bivalent vaccine, in adults who had completed a primary vaccination series with or without a booster. The study found that all vaccines elicited robust immune responses, with no serious adverse events or myocarditis/pericarditis cases reported. CD4+ T cells increased in all groups, while CD8+ T cells increased in all groups except the lowest CV0701 dose group. The results suggest that these vaccines are safe and immunogenic, comparable to the licensed vaccine. However, the study was limited to healthy adults and lacked long-term follow-up, which may affect generalizability. The evidence is strong due to the controlled design and comprehensive immune response evaluation.

title: Convalescent Plasma Restores Viral Clearance After Anti-Spike Monoclonal Antibody Failure in Immunocompromised COVID-19 Patients: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Individual Patient Data.
abstract: Anti-Spike monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) progressively lost efficacy during the COVID-19 pandemic due to the emergence and predominance of resistant SARS-CoV-2 variants. By contrast, high-titre COVID-19 convalescent plasma (CCP) collected from vaccinated donors recently recovered from infection provides a polyclonal source of antibodies that remains effective in clearing SARS-CoV-2 in immunosuppressed patients, unable to mount an adequate immune response against the virus. We conducted a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis to examine the effect of CCP in immunocompromised patients persistently positive for SARS-CoV-2 viraemia following mAb therapy, and to evaluate possible biological factors associated with a favourable outcome. Electronic databases were searched for studies published from January 2020 to January 2026. All studies including eligible cases were considered in the systematic review. Unpublished cases were also collected from investigators of the selected studies. The protocol was registered at PROSPERO (CRD420251142891). Forty-seven cases (30 cases from 12 published studies and 17 unpublished cases) were included. In 33 out of 47 patients (70.2%) with a mAb-resistant infection, SARS-CoV-2 clearance occurred following CCP transfusion, with a mean of 2.7 CCP units administered. In logistic regression, total CCP volume transfused was positively associated with SARS-CoV-2 clearance. In conclusion, CCP transfusion was associated with SARS-CoV-2 clearance in persistently positive immunocompromised patients following failure of anti-Spike mAb therapy.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines the efficacy of high-titre COVID-19 convalescent plasma (CCP) in restoring viral clearance among immunocompromised patients with persistent SARS-CoV-2 viraemia following failure of anti-Spike monoclonal antibody (mAb) therapy, focusing on the central question of whether CCP can overcome resistance to mAbs in this population.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis was conducted, searching electronic databases from January 2020 to January 2026. The protocol was registered at PROSPERO (CRD420251142891). Forty-seven cases (30 from 12 published studies and 17 unpublished cases) were included, with eligibility criteria encompassing immunocompromised patients persistently positive for SARS-CoV-2 after mAb therapy.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that CCP transfusion was associated with SARS-CoV-2 clearance in 70.2% (33/47) of immunocompromised patients with mAb-resistant infections, with a mean of 2.7 CCP units administered. Total CCP volume transfused was positively associated with viral clearance in logistic regression analysis.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not report long-term outcomes, durability of viral clearance, or comparative efficacy against newer antiviral agents. Additionally, the small sample size (47 cases) and reliance on unpublished cases limit generalizability and robustness of conclusions.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review highlights the need for randomized controlled trials to validate CCP efficacy in immunocompromised populations and to determine optimal dosing strategies. analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated convalescent plasma (CCP) as a rescue therapy for immunocompromised COVID-19 patients with persistent SARS-CoV-2 viraemia after anti-Spike monoclonal antibody (mAb) failure. Across 47 cases, CCP achieved viral clearance in 70.2% of patients, with higher transfusion volumes correlating with improved outcomes. The review underscores CCP's potential role in overcoming mAb resistance but emphasizes the need for larger, controlled studies to confirm efficacy, optimize dosing, and assess long-term durability. Given the limited sample size and reliance on unpublished data, findings should be interpreted cautiously.

title: Immunological effects of supervised exercise in long COVID in adults: A secondary analysis of a randomized crossover trial
abstract: Abstract Long COVID (post‐acute sequelae of SARS‐CoV‐2 infection) affects approximately 5%–30% of survivors and is characterized by persistent fatigue, dyspnea, exercise intolerance, and cognitive impairment. We evaluated the immunological effects of supervised exercise in adults with long COVID. In this pre‐specified exploratory substudy of the EXER‐COVID randomized 2 × 2 crossover trial, participants completed a 6‐week supervised exercise program (twice weekly) or usual care before crossing over after a 3–5 day washout. Plasma cytokines (IL‐1β, IL‐6, IL‐10, TNF‐α, MCP‐1/CCL2, MIP‐1α/CCL3, MIP‐1β/CCL4, and IP‐10/CXCL10) were measured by multiplex immunoassay. Immunophenotyping included 20 CD4 + and CD8 + T‐cell subsets and five innate immune populations. Treatment effects were estimated using within‐period change scores, with multiple testing controlled by the Benjamini–Hochberg procedure (false discovery rate < 5%). Five variables reached nominal significance before correction (two CD8 + T‐cell subsets and IL‐1β, IL‐10, and MIP‐1α), but none remained significant after adjustment. No changes were observed in innate immune populations, and no evidence of carryover was detected. Supervised exercise was not associated with significant immunological changes after correction for multiple comparisons, supporting the short‐term immunological safety of moderate‐intensity exercise in PESE‐negative adults with long COVID ( ClinicalTrials.gov : NCT04797871).

title: Psychoeducational Challenges of Dyslexic Children During the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Dyslexic students faced psychological and educational challenges during the COVID-19 pandemic and online learning, including increased anxiety, low self-esteem, reduced reading interest, limited access to educational technologies, insufficient teacher support, and difficulties with reading fluency and concentration. Examining these challenges is crucial for implementing effective measures and enhancing post-pandemic learning. This study investigates the psycho-educational challenges of dyslexic children during the pandemic, highlighting the need for targeted interventions to support them in current and future contexts. This systematic review identified relevant articles through electronic searches of PubMed, Wiley, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and ScienceDirect, supplemented by the snowballing technique, which involved examining the bibliographies of retrieved references. The study identified two main categories of challenges for dyslexic children: psychological (mental health, emotional well-being, behavioural issues, parental stress) and educational (socioeconomic status, technology access, special educational needs, teacher support, remote learning difficulties) affecting children with learning disabilities. The research results show that dyslexic children faced various psychological and educational difficulties identified in this review during the COVID-19 pandemic. Therefore, targeted, evidence-based strategies-such as teacher training, family-school collaboration, adaptive learning technologies, and psychological support-are needed to mitigate these challenges in the post-pandemic period.

title: Timing, Titre, and Host Determinants of Convalescent Plasma Efficacy in COVID-19: A Systematic Review With Design-Stratified Narrative Synthesis.
abstract: The efficacy of convalescent plasma (CP) in COVID-19 has been contested, with large randomized trials producing conflicting results that led to recommendations against routine use. We performed a systematic review with design-stratified narrative synthesis (PRISMA 2020; SWiM; OSF: https://osf.io/tjcuq) to test whether these conflicting outcomes can be reconciled through three interacting determinants-timing, antibody titre, and host characteristics-using a standardized 91-field extraction matrix applied to each study. PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched through May 2026. Thirty-one studies (20,793 patients; 8 RCTs, 23 observational) were included. The synthesis indicates that CP is effective, but only under a specific convergence of conditions: when administered early in the disease course, with sufficient antibody titre, to seronegative or immunocompromised hosts who have not yet mounted an endogenous antibody response. Among RCTs analysing timing, 4 of 6 found benefit with earlier administration; for titre, 3 of 4 RCTs with explicit comparisons found benefit with higher-titre CP; and two large RCTs (combined n = 12,522) demonstrated preferential benefit in seronegative recipients. This interpretation is consistent with modelling estimates that CP, deployed largely to hospitalised patients, nonetheless saved tens of thousands of lives in the United States during the first pandemic year, an effect attributed to the subset treated early enough to modify disease progression. A second, previously unquantified finding concerns antibody class: characterisation of non-IgG immunoglobulins was nearly absent, with only 2 of 31 studies-both from our group-reporting IgA or IgM data, despite evidence that IgA and IgM are among the most potent neutralising classes against SARS-CoV-2. This hypothesis-generating observation identifies a systematic gap in CP product assessment. These findings reframe CP efficacy from a binary question to a conditional one and provide a template for the precision deployment of passive immunotherapy in future pandemics.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines the efficacy of convalescent plasma (CP) for COVID-19 caused by SARS-CoV-2, focusing on three interacting determinants: timing of administration, antibody titre, and host characteristics, to reconcile conflicting trial outcomes.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A systematic review with design-stratified narrative synthesis (PRISMA 2020; SWiM) was conducted, searching PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus through May 2026, applying a standardized 91-field extraction matrix to 31 included studies (20,793 patients; 8 RCTs, 23 observational).
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: CP is effective only under specific conditions: early administration, sufficient antibody titre, and in seronegative or immunocompromised hosts lacking endogenous antibody responses. Among RCTs, 4 of 6 found benefit with earlier administration, 3 of 4 with higher-titre CP, and two large RCTs (n=12,522) showed preferential benefit in seronegative recipients.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Characterisation of non-IgG immunoglobulins (IgA/IgM) in CP products is nearly absent, with only 2 of 31 studies reporting such data despite evidence of their potent neutralising activity against SARS-CoV-2, representing a systematic gap in product assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review resolves conflicting evidence on convalescent plasma (CP) efficacy in COVID-19 by identifying three critical determinants: early administration, high antibody titre, and host seronegativity or immunocompromise. Among 31 studies (20,793 patients), randomized trials showed benefit when CP was given early (4/6 trials) or with higher titres (3/4 trials), particularly in seronegative recipients (two large RCTs, n=12,522). However, a major evidence gap persists: only 2 studies assessed non-IgG immunoglobulins (IgA/IgM), despite their potential potency. The review reframes CP efficacy as conditional and provides a template for precision deployment in future pandemics, emphasizing the need for standardized IgA/IgM quantification and targeted clinical strategies.

title_zh: Timing, Titre, and Host Determinants of Convalescent Plasma Efficacy in COVID-19: A Systematic Review With Design-Stratified Narrative Synthesis.
source_body_en: The efficacy of convalescent plasma (CP) in COVID-19 has been contested, with large randomized trials producing conflicting results that led to recommendations against routine use. We performed a systematic review with design-stratified narrative synthesis (PRISMA 2020; SWiM; OSF: https://osf.io/tjcuq) to test whether these conflicting outcomes can be reconciled through three interacting determinants-timing, antibody titre, and host characteristics-using a standardized 91-field extraction matrix applied to each study. PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched through May 2026. Thirty-one studies (20,793 patients; 8 RCTs, 23 observational) were included. The synthesis indicates that CP is effective, but only under a specific convergence of conditions: when administered early in the disease course, with sufficient antibody titre, to seronegative or immunocompromised hosts who have not yet mounted an endogenous antibody response. Among RCTs analysing timing, 4 of 6 found benefit with earlier administration; for titre, 3 of 4 RCTs with explicit comparisons found benefit with higher-titre CP; and two large RCTs (combined n = 12,522) demonstrated preferential benefit in seronegative recipients. This interpretation is consistent with modelling estimates that CP, deployed largely to hospitalised patients, nonetheless saved tens of thousands of lives in the United States during the first pandemic year, an effect attributed to the subset treated early enough to modify disease progression. A second, previously unquantified finding concerns antibody class: characterisation of non-IgG immunoglobulins was nearly absent, with only 2 of 31 studies-both from our group-reporting IgA or IgM data, despite evidence that IgA and IgM are among the most potent neutralising classes against SARS-CoV-2. This hypothesis-generating observation identifies a systematic gap in CP product assessment. These findings reframe CP efficacy from a binary question to a conditional one and provide a template for the precision deployment of passive immunotherapy in future pandemics.

title: Molecular Epidemiology of Emerging Subvariants of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron Lineage: A Cross-sectional Study from Himachal Pradesh, India
abstract: Introduction: Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) shows continuous genetic variation, resulting in the emergence of multiple viral lineages worldwide. These mutations can influence viral transmissibility, pathogenic potential, and immune escape, resulting in changed disease pattern. Genomic surveillance allows systematic tracking of viral evolution and circulating variants; thus, monitoring is essential for informed public health planning and clinical preparedness. Aim: To detect the emergence of variants of Omicron lineage in the hilly state of Himachal Pradesh, India. Materials and Methods: This cross-sectional study was conducted at the Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri Medical College, Mandi, Himachal Pradesh, India from January 2024 to June 2024. All the SARS-CoV-2 positive samples with Ct value ≤30 received across the state from the four Virus Research and Diagnostic Laboratories (VRDLs) of the state were included. Ribonucleic acid (RNA) extraction was performed using the Q-Line Molecular Viral RNA Extraction Kit, and Whole Genome Sequencing (WGS) was carried out on the Oxford Nanopore MinION platform. Consensus sequences were generated using Medaka and Nanopolish for variant identification and phylogenetic analysis. All demographic and clinical data, like age, sex, clinical presentation, and vaccination status, were recorded and tabulated in Microsoft Excel 2021. The study focused on genomic sequences generated, and the data were presented as numbers and percentages. Results: A total of 30 SARS-CoV-2 positive samples were received. Among SARS-CoV-2 positive cases, adult females constituted the highest proportion, 17 (56.7%), with most patients aged 19-60 years, 17 (56.7%), and the majority of samples originating from Shimla, 11 (36.7%). The study identified JN.1 sublineages in 19 (63.3%) as the predominant cause of infection. Most cases, 20 (66.7%) reported to the outpatient department. Mild symptoms such as fever and cough were seen in 7 (35%) cases. Even though 23 (76.7%) of cases were vaccinated with the COVID-19 vaccine, 10 (33.3%) required admissions. However, no mortality was reported. Conclusion: Tracking SARS-CoV-2 variants revealed the predominance of the JN.1 sublineage of Omicron with generally mild symptoms. Continuous genetic evolution of SARS CoV-2 highlights the need for robust, ongoing genomic surveillance integrated with epidemiological data to enable early detection of emerging variants and strengthen control strategies.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 的持续遗传变异推动了新发系统的出现,这些系统可能影响传播力、致病性和免疫逃逸,从而需要对流行变异株进行监测以支撑公共卫生规划。本研究旨在检测印度喜马偕尔邦出现的奥密克戎变异株亚谱系,以填补当地 基因组监测 的数据缺口。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本横断面研究于2024年1月至2024年6月在印度喜马偕尔邦曼迪市的Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri医学院开展。纳入了来自该邦四家病毒研究与诊断实验室且Ct值≤30的严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2阳性样本。
elements_zh.methods: 使用 Q-Line Molecular 病毒 RNA 提取试剂盒进行 RNA 提取,并在 Oxford Nanopore MinION 平台上完成了 基因组 的全基因组测序。使用 Medaka 和 Nanopolish 生成共识序列,用于变异识别与系统发育分析。
elements_zh.main_results: 共收到30份严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2阳性样本,其中成年女性占56.7%(17/30),大多数患者年龄在19–60岁(56.7%,17/30)。样本主要来自喜马偕尔邦(36.7%,11/30),且63.3%(19/30)的病例中检测出JN.1亚谱系。大多数病例(66.7%,20/30)在门诊就诊,其中35%(7/20)出现轻微症状如发热和咳嗽。尽管76.7%(23/30)已完成疫苗接种,但仍有33.3%(10/30)需要住院,未报告死亡率病例。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在测序病例中,JN.1亚谱系占据主导地位,表明奥密克戎亚变异株在当地持续传播,且临床表现通常较轻。该研究强调了基因组监测在区域环境中检测新兴变异株的实用性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现支持将 基因组监测 与流行病学数据相结合,以实现新兴 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变异株的早期检测,并加强丘陵地区的本地控制策略。JN.1 的优势地位凸显了针对性公共卫生应对措施的必要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 样本量较小(n=30)且为单中心设计,限制了结果的普遍性;依赖Ct值≤30可能引入选择偏倚。由于横断面设计及未控制混杂因素,证据强度为中等。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 的持续遗传变异推动了新发系统的出现,这些系统可能影响传播力、致病性和免疫逃逸,从而需要对流行变异株进行监测以支撑公共卫生规划。本研究旨在检测印度喜马偕尔邦出现的奥密克戎变异株亚谱系,以填补当地 基因组监测 的数据缺口。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本横断面研究于2024年1月至2024年6月在印度喜马偕尔邦曼迪市的Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri医学院开展。纳入了来自该邦四家病毒研究与诊断实验室且Ct值≤30的严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2阳性样本。
analysis_zh.methods: 使用 Q-Line Molecular 病毒 RNA 提取试剂盒进行 RNA 提取,并在 Oxford Nanopore MinION 平台上完成了 基因组 的全基因组测序。使用 Medaka 和 Nanopolish 生成共识序列,用于变异识别与系统发育分析。
analysis_zh.main_results: 共收到30份严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2阳性样本,其中成年女性占56.7%(17/30),大多数患者年龄在19–60岁(56.7%,17/30)。样本主要来自喜马偕尔邦(36.7%,11/30),且63.3%(19/30)的病例中检测出JN.1亚谱系。大多数病例(66.7%,20/30)在门诊就诊,其中35%(7/20)出现轻微症状如发热和咳嗽。尽管76.7%(23/30)已完成疫苗接种,但仍有33.3%(10/30)需要住院,未报告死亡率病例。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在测序病例中,JN.1亚谱系占据主导地位,表明奥密克戎亚变异株在当地持续传播,且临床表现通常较轻。该研究强调了基因组监测在区域环境中检测新兴变异株的实用性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现支持将 基因组监测 与流行病学数据相结合,以实现新兴 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变异株的早期检测,并加强丘陵地区的本地控制策略。JN.1 的优势地位凸显了针对性公共卫生应对措施的必要性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 样本量较小(n=30)且为单中心设计,限制了结果的普遍性;依赖Ct值≤30可能引入选择偏倚。由于横断面设计及未控制混杂因素,证据强度为中等。

title: High levels of cell-free hemoglobin and iron in cerebral thrombi of pre-Omicron COVID-19 stroke patients: novel drivers of SARS-CoV-2–induced prothrombotic state
abstract: The pathophysiological mechanisms underlying the hypercoagulable state and thrombotic events associated with COVID-19 remain incompletely understood. To investigate prothrombotic alterations during SARS-CoV-2 infection, we performed an exploratory and integrated analysis of cerebral thrombi retrieved, during the first wave of the pandemic, by mechanical thrombectomy from stroke patients with (n=6) and without (n=6) COVID-19. We combined histological and ultrastructural assessment with quantitative proteomics and elemental profiling to identify differences in cellular organization and in protein and metal composition. Immunohistochemical quantification revealed a trend toward increased macrophage abundance, a more diffuse CD68+ staining pattern, and reduced platelet content in COVID-19 thrombi. In contrast, neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) burden, neutrophil number, and erythrocyte content did not differ significantly between groups. Transmission electron microscopy showed a disorganized ultrastructural fibrillar network in thrombi from COVID-19 stroke patients, consistent with the irregular and less densely packed extracellular matrix observed by Masson's trichrome staining. Furthermore, quantitative proteomics by liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (LC–MS/MS) identified 48 differentially expressed proteins among 720 shared proteins, with marked upregulation of hemoglobin subunits (α, β, γ, and δ), haptoglobin, biliverdin reductase and redox-regulating proteins, alongside downregulation of platelet-related proteins in COVID-19 thrombi. Total reflection X-ray fluorescence (TXRF) confirmed increased iron levels in COVID-19-associated thrombi. Notably, glycophorin A immunostaining did not indicate increased erythrocyte abundance, and erythrocyte structural proteins were not differentially expressed in proteomic analysis, suggesting that hemoglobin and iron were largely present in a cell-free form within the retrieved thrombi of COVID-19 stroke patients. In addition, acute-phase reactants, classical complement components, and immunoglobulins were detected exclusively in COVID-19 samples, consistent with a distinctive immune-inflammatory and oxidative signature. Overall, these findings support a novel pathophysiological mechanism underlying COVID-19-associated hypercoagulability and thrombosis, involving elevated circulating cell-free hemoglobin and increased iron content. Furthermore, this study highlights the potential contribution of hemoglobin/iron-related processes to the COVID-19 prothrombotic state and may provide molecular targets for future therapeutic strategies.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the incomplete understanding of mechanisms driving the hypercoagulable state and thrombotic events in COVID-19, aiming to identify novel prothrombotic alterations associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection.
analysis.study_design_and_population: An exploratory, integrated analysis was conducted on cerebral thrombi retrieved by mechanical thrombectomy from six stroke patients with COVID-19 and six without COVID-19 during the first pandemic wave.
analysis.methods: Histological and ultrastructural assessments were combined with quantitative proteomics (LC–MS/MS) and elemental profiling (TXRF) to compare cellular organization, protein composition, and metal content between thrombi from COVID-19 and non-COVID-19 patients.
analysis.main_results: COVID-19 thrombi showed a trend toward increased macrophage abundance and diffuse CD68+ staining, reduced platelet content, and a disorganized fibrillar network. Proteomics identified 48 differentially expressed proteins among 720 shared proteins, with upregulation of hemoglobin subunits, haptoglobin, biliverdin reductase, and redox-regulating proteins, and downregulation of platelet-related proteins. TXRF confirmed increased iron levels, while glycophorin A immunostaining and erythrocyte structural proteins indicated cell-free hemoglobin and iron presence.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret these findings as supporting a novel mechanism for COVID-19-associated hypercoagulability involving elevated cell-free hemoglobin and iron, distinct from NETs burden or erythrocyte abundance. They highlight the identification of hemoglobin/iron-related processes as a potential molecular target for future therapies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that hemoglobin and iron dysregulation may contribute to the prothrombotic state in COVID-19, potentially informing diagnostic or therapeutic strategies targeting these pathways in stroke patients with SARS-CoV-2 infection.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The small sample size (n=6 per group) and exploratory design limit generalizability and causal inference. The study relies on thrombi retrieved during a specific pandemic wave, which may not represent later variants or broader populations, warranting cautious interpretation.

analysis.summary_en: This exploratory study investigated prothrombotic alterations in cerebral thrombi from COVID-19 stroke patients compared to non-COVID-19 controls during the first pandemic wave. Using histological, ultrastructural, proteomic, and elemental analyses, the authors identified increased cell-free hemoglobin and iron levels in COVID-19 thrombi, alongside reduced platelet content and a disorganized fibrillar network. Proteomics revealed upregulation of hemoglobin subunits, haptoglobin, and redox-regulating proteins, with downregulation of platelet-related proteins. These findings support a novel mechanism for COVID-19-associated hypercoagulability distinct from NETs or erythrocyte abundance. While the study provides mechanistic insights, its small sample size and focus on early pandemic thrombi limit generalizability and preclude causal conclusions.

elements_en.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the incomplete understanding of mechanisms driving the hypercoagulable state and thrombotic events in COVID-19, aiming to identify novel prothrombotic alterations associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: An exploratory, integrated analysis was conducted on cerebral thrombi retrieved by mechanical thrombectomy from six stroke patients with COVID-19 and six without COVID-19 during the first pandemic wave.
elements_en.methods: Histological and ultrastructural assessments were combined with quantitative proteomics (LC–MS/MS) and elemental profiling (TXRF) to compare cellular organization, protein composition, and metal content between thrombi from COVID-19 and non-COVID-19 patients.
elements_en.main_results: COVID-19 thrombi showed a trend toward increased macrophage abundance and diffuse CD68+ staining, reduced platelet content, and a disorganized fibrillar network. Proteomics identified 48 differentially expressed proteins among 720 shared proteins, with upregulation of hemoglobin subunits, haptoglobin, biliverdin reductase, and redox-regulating proteins, and downregulation of platelet-related proteins. TXRF confirmed increased iron levels, while glycophorin A immunostaining and erythrocyte structural proteins indicated cell-free hemoglobin and iron presence.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret these findings as supporting a novel mechanism for COVID-19-associated hypercoagulability involving elevated cell-free hemoglobin and iron, distinct from NETs burden or erythrocyte abundance. They highlight the identification of hemoglobin/iron-related processes as a potential molecular target for future therapies.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that hemoglobin and iron dysregulation may contribute to the prothrombotic state in COVID-19, potentially informing diagnostic or therapeutic strategies targeting these pathways in stroke patients with SARS-CoV-2 infection.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The small sample size (n=6 per group) and exploratory design limit generalizability and causal inference. The study relies on thrombi retrieved during a specific pandemic wave, which may not represent later variants or broader populations, warranting cautious interpretation.

title_zh: High levels of cell-free hemoglobin and iron in cerebral thrombi of pre-Omicron COVID-19 stroke patients: novel drivers of SARS-CoV-2–induced prothrombotic state
source_body_en: The pathophysiological mechanisms underlying the hypercoagulable state and thrombotic events associated with COVID-19 remain incompletely understood. To investigate prothrombotic alterations during SARS-CoV-2 infection, we performed an exploratory and integrated analysis of cerebral thrombi retrieved, during the first wave of the pandemic, by mechanical thrombectomy from stroke patients with (n=6) and without (n=6) COVID-19. We combined histological and ultrastructural assessment with quantitative proteomics and elemental profiling to identify differences in cellular organization and in protein and metal composition. Immunohistochemical quantification revealed a trend toward increased macrophage abundance, a more diffuse CD68+ staining pattern, and reduced platelet content in COVID-19 thrombi. In contrast, neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) burden, neutrophil number, and erythrocyte content did not differ significantly between groups. Transmission electron microscopy showed a disorganized ultrastructural fibrillar network in thrombi from COVID-19 stroke patients, consistent with the irregular and less densely packed extracellular matrix observed by Masson's trichrome staining. Furthermore, quantitative proteomics by liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (LC–MS/MS) identified 48 differentially expressed proteins among 720 shared proteins, with marked upregulation of hemoglobin subunits (α, β, γ, and δ), haptoglobin, biliverdin reductase and redox-regulating proteins, alongside downregulation of platelet-related proteins in COVID-19 thrombi. Total reflection X-ray fluorescence (TXRF) confirmed increased iron levels in COVID-19-associated thrombi. Notably, glycophorin A immunostaining did not indicate increased erythrocyte abundance, and erythrocyte structural proteins were not differentially expressed in proteomic analysis, suggesting that hemoglobin and iron were largely present in a cell-free form within the retrieved thrombi of COVID-19 stroke patients. In addition, acute-phase reactants, classical complement components, and immunoglobulins were detected exclusively in COVID-19 samples, consistent with a distinctive immune-inflammatory and oxidative signature. Overall, these findings support a novel pathophysiological mechanism underlying COVID-19-associated hypercoagulability and thrombosis, involving elevated circulating cell-free hemoglobin and increased iron content. Furthermore, this study highlights the potential contribution of hemoglobin/iron-related processes to the COVID-19 prothrombotic state and may provide molecular targets for future therapeutic strategies.

title: Engineering antigenic breadth against SARS-CoV-2 by pairing divergent RBDs within a single mRNA immunogen.
abstract: Vaccines capable of eliciting broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) are a major goal for pandemic preparedness. A challenge across vaccine fields is how to deliberately recruit the rare B cell clones that recognize conserved epitopes shared across diverse viral variants. BnAbs have been known to frequently emerge through extensive somatic hypermutation during affinity maturation, here we describe an alternative mechanism for bnAb selection. We designed an mRNA vaccine in which two antigenically distinct (severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2) SARS-CoV-2 variant's (Omicron and Delta; O-Δ) receptor binding domains (RBDs) are physically fused on a single polypeptide. This design is predicted to favor B cell antigen receptors capable of engaging conserved epitopes on both RBDs with enhanced avidity. A matched nondivergent tandem RBD (Delta-Delta; Δ-Δ) served as a control. In mice, immunization elicited potent antibody responses and increased the frequency of cross-reactive B cells, recognizing Delta, Omicron, and the 2002 pandemic strain SARS-CoV RBDs. Using multicolor RBD tetramers and single-cell B cell receptor sequencing, we show that breadth arises via two distinct pathways. The divergent vaccine preferentially enriches clonally distinct cross-reactive B cells (not present within non-cross-reactive B cell pools) with low levels of somatic hypermutation, consistent with selection of germline-biased precursors. In contrast, the matched control vaccine yields cross-reactivity primarily within existing clonal lineages (clonal overlap between cross-reactive and non-cross-reactive cells) and at higher mutational burdens, consistent with affinity-maturation-driven acquisition of breadth. This work establishes a simple, modular antigen-design principle in which juxtaposing appropriately divergent antigens on a single scaffold promotes the enrichment of bnAb-prone B cells.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

title: The Role of Community Health Workers in Increasing Access to Essential Health and Social Services During the COVID-19 Pandemic.
abstract: To describe the health care and social services needs addressed by community health workers (CHWs) through referrals in the Community Health Workers for COVID-19 Response and Resilient Communities (CCR) program. We performed a descriptive analysis of national performance measure data from 67 CCR recipients from 2021 to 2024 documenting referrals, alongside 2 web-based surveys of 63 program administrators and 689 CHWs in the United States in early 2024. CHWs made 464 158 social and 323 769 health referrals, with 282 596 referrals completed. Referrals included services for food, housing, legal assistance, health insurance, lifestyle interventions, chronic disease management, COVID-19‒related care, and maternal and child health care. Referral success was aided by community resources, CHW knowledge, and networking, and limited by costs, mistrust, language barriers, transportation, and child care challenges. CHWs connect individuals to health care and provide follow-up care and social support. Comprehensive and coordinated health and social services are essential to optimize the referral and service delivery. Public Health Implications. Findings support policies promoting the integration, expansion, and sustainability of the CHW workforce. (Am J Public Health. 2026;116(S4):S331-S340. https://doi.org/10.2105/AJPH.2026.308642).

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates the role of community health workers (CHWs) in addressing health and social service needs during the COVID-19 pandemic through the Community Health Workers for COVID-19 Response and Resilient Communities (CCR) program. The analysis combines national performance measure data from 67 CCR recipients (2021–2024) with web-based surveys of 63 program administrators and 689 CHWs in the United States. CHWs made 464,158 social and 323,769 health referrals, with 282,596 completed. Referral success was influenced by community resources, CHW knowledge, and networking, but constrained by costs, mistrust, language barriers, transportation, and child care challenges. The review highlights the importance of CHWs in connecting individuals to health care and providing follow-up support, emphasizing the need for comprehensive and coordinated services. Findings advocate for policies that integrate, expand, and sustain the CHW workforce to improve access to essential health and social services during public health crises.

title: The Impact of Setting Characteristics on Community Health Worker Roles and COVID-19 Activities: An Examination of the Community Health Workers for COVID Response and Resilient Communities Program.
abstract: To examine the roles and activities performed by community health workers (CHWs) involved in the national Community Health Workers for COVID Response and Resilient Communities (CCR) program and examine differences based on setting characteristics. We used data from a CHW self-report survey (n = 689) conducted February through March 2024 in the United States. We ran a series of ordered logistic regression models to examine the association between setting characteristics (i.e., type of organizational setting, organizational experience with CHWs, and populations of focus) and CHW core roles and COVID-19‒specific activities. A total of 69.2% of CHWs in the analytic sample reported performing all 10 core roles. Organizational experience with CHWs and populations of focus emerged as the most salient predictors of CHW core roles and activities. A substantial proportion of CHWs performed the full range of core roles. Results suggest that CHWs in the CCR program tailored their roles and activities according to the unique factors of the communities in which they worked. Public Health Implications. Programs such as CCR may result in CHWs using a wide range of core roles across multiple settings. (Am J Public Health. 2026;116(S4):S295-S304. https://doi.org/10.2105/AJPH.2026.308660).

analysis.summary_en: This review article examines the roles and activities of community health workers (CHWs) in the Community Health Workers for COVID Response and Resilient Communities (CCR) program, focusing on how setting characteristics influence their functions. The study used data from a self-report survey of 689 CHWs conducted in the United States between February and March 2024. Ordered logistic regression models were employed to analyze the relationship between organizational settings, experience with CHWs, and populations of focus with CHW roles and activities. The findings indicate that 69.2% of CHWs performed all 10 core roles, and their activities were tailored to the unique factors of their communities. Organizational experience and population focus were identified as the most significant predictors of CHW roles and activities. The study highlights the importance of context-specific approaches in CHW programs and suggests implications for public health strategies.

title: Evaluating the Potential Influence of Federal COVID-19 Response Funding on the Building and Sustainability of the CHW Workforce.
abstract: To describe the potential influence of Community Health Workers for COVID-19 Response and Resilient Communities (CCR) funding on community health worker (CHW) hiring, retention, and workforce sustainability. A descriptive analysis of a cross-sectional, web-based survey of directors and coordinators of 63 CCR recipient organizations administered between February and March 2024 was conducted in the United States. Survey questions assessed program funding sources, payment mechanisms for CHW services, and CHW hiring and retention. About 65% of CCR recipients relied solely on CCR funds, whereas others leveraged over $117 million in additional funding, mostly federal, to support CCR program implementation. Of 1359 CHW positions supported by CCR, respondents expected to maintain 749. Recipients planned to use grant funding and Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services reimbursement as strategies for retention. Federal funding can contribute meaningfully to sustaining CHW employment across different settings, yet sustainability of this vital public health workforce is not assured. Public Health Implications. The findings underscore the importance of long-term investment via diverse funding sources and building programmatic capacity to strengthen and sustain the CHW workforce. (Am J Public Health. 2026;116(S4):S321-S330. https://doi.org/10.2105/AJPH.2026.308646).

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates the influence of federal funding on the sustainability of the community health worker (CHW) workforce in the context of the Community Health Workers for COVID-19 Response and Resilient Communities (CCR) program. A cross-sectional survey of 63 CCR recipient organizations was conducted between February and March 2024, assessing funding sources, payment mechanisms, and CHW hiring and retention. The findings indicate that 65% of recipients relied solely on CCR funds, while others used additional federal funding. Of 1359 CHW positions, 749 were expected to be maintained. Retention strategies included grant funding and Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services reimbursement. The review highlights the need for long-term investment and programmatic capacity to ensure CHW workforce sustainability, though federal funding alone may not guarantee it.

title: A Community Health Worker-Led Model of Training and Technical Assistance to Support National Community Health Worker Program Implementation for COVID-19 Response: United States, 2021-2025.
abstract: To assess training and technical assistance (TTA) needs among 67 Centers for Disease Control and Prevention-funded community health worker (CHW) programs in the United States and to assess the reach of a national CHW-led TTA program designed to meet the needs identified. From December 2021 through January 2022, we assessed TTA needs through an online survey and interviews with program staff. We used findings to inform TTA content and delivery. From 2021 through 2025, we collected participation data to assess program reach. Among 59 survey respondents and representatives from 10 organizations, funding recipients identified hiring, program implementation, financial sustainability, and peer learning as priorities for TTA. Based on these findings, we developed webinars, communities of practice, leadership training, and individualized TTA. The program reached all funded recipients and generated 8824 participant encounters, 54.7% of whom were CHWs. Health departments implementing CHW programs demonstrated substantial demand for and engagement in CHW-led TTA. Policymakers should prioritize sustained investment in TTA infrastructure to support implementation and long-term sustainability of CHW programs. (Am J Public Health. 2026;116(S4):S314-S320. https://doi.org/10.2105/AJPH.2026.308665).

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines the training and technical assistance (TTA) needs of community health worker (CHW) programs in the United States during the COVID-19 response, focusing on the implementation and reach of a national CHW-led TTA program to support these programs from 2021 to 2025.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review describes an online survey and interviews conducted from December 2021 through January 2022 to assess TTA needs among 67 CDC-funded CHW programs, using findings to inform TTA content and delivery. Participation data were collected from 2021 through 2025 to assess program reach.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that health departments implementing CHW programs demonstrated substantial demand for and engagement in CHW-led TTA, with the program reaching all funded recipients and generating 8824 participant encounters, 54.7% of whom were CHWs.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The supplied evidence does not report heterogeneity in TTA needs across regions, populations, or program types, nor does it address conflicting findings or unresolved mechanisms related to CHW-led TTA effectiveness.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review implies that policymakers should prioritize sustained investment in TTA infrastructure to support the implementation and long-term sustainability of CHW programs, particularly in funding, hiring, program implementation, financial sustainability, and peer learning.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates a national community health worker (CHW)-led training and technical assistance (TTA) program designed to support U.S. CHW programs during the COVID-19 response (2021–2025). Using survey and interview data from December 2021–January 2022, the program identified hiring, program implementation, financial sustainability, and peer learning as key TTA priorities. Based on these findings, the program developed webinars, communities of practice, leadership training, and individualized TTA. By 2025, the program reached all funded recipients, generating 8824 participant encounters, with 54.7% involving CHWs. The review highlights substantial demand for and engagement in CHW-led TTA among health departments, underscoring the need for sustained investment in TTA infrastructure to ensure program implementation and long-term sustainability.

title: Cytokine-Driven Hyperinflammation in Long COVID: Mechanisms, Biomarkers, Complement Dysregulation, and Emerging Immunotherapies-A Narrative Review.
abstract: ABSTRACT Background and Aims Long COVID, also known as post‐acute sequelae of SARS‐CoV‐2 infection (PASC), is a multisystem condition characterized by persistent symptoms that continue beyond the acute phase of infection. Growing evidence indicates that sustained immune dysregulation involving cytokine‐mediated inflammation, complement activation, endothelial dysfunction, thromboinflammation, and viral antigen persistence contributes to its pathogenesis. This narrative review summarizes current evidence on the mechanisms underlying hyperinflammation in Long COVID, highlights emerging biomarkers, and evaluates evolving immunotherapeutic strategies. Methods A narrative literature search was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and Google Scholar for studies published between 2020 and 2026. Priority was given to systematic reviews, meta‐analyses, cohort studies, mechanistic investigations, and clinical trials examining immune dysregulation, inflammatory biomarkers, complement pathways, and targeted therapies in long COVID. Results Persistent elevation of pro‐inflammatory cytokines, including interleukin‐6, interleukin‐1β, tumor necrosis factor‐α, interferon‐γ, and interleukin‐17, together with activation of the alternative and lectin complement pathways, contributes to endothelial injury, microvascular thrombosis, neuroinflammation, fibrosis, and multisystem dysfunction. Emerging biomarkers include inflammatory cytokines, complement proteins, endothelial activation markers, coagulation indices, and multi‐omics signatures that may improve disease stratification and therapeutic monitoring. Investigational therapies include cytokine‐targeted biologics, complement inhibitors, Janus kinase inhibitors, mesenchymal stem cell therapy, microbiome‐directed interventions, and precision immunotherapy. Conclusion Long COVID results from complex interactions between persistent inflammation, complement dysregulation, vascular injury, and immune dysfunction. Integrating validated biomarkers with precision immunotherapeutic approaches may improve diagnosis, risk stratification, and individualized management. However, robust prospective studies and randomized clinical trials remain essential to validate these strategies and optimize long‐term clinical outcomes.

analysis.summary_en: This narrative review explores the mechanisms of cytokine-driven hyperinflammation in Long COVID, focusing on persistent immune dysregulation, complement activation, and vascular injury. The review synthesizes evidence from studies published between 2020 and 2026, sourced from PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and Google Scholar. It highlights the role of pro-inflammatory cytokines such as interleukin-6, interleukin-1β, tumor necrosis factor-α, interferon-γ, and interleukin-17, as well as the alternative and lectin complement pathways, in contributing to multisystem dysfunction. The review also identifies emerging biomarkers that may enhance disease stratification and therapeutic monitoring, and suggests that integrating these biomarkers with precision immunotherapies could improve diagnosis and management. However, the review emphasizes the need for robust prospective studies and randomized clinical trials to validate these strategies and optimize long-term outcomes.

elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本研究通过PubMed、Scopus、Web of Science、Embase及Google Scholar数据库检索2020年至2026年间发表的文献。优先纳入系统性综述、荟萃分析、病例报告、机制研究及临床试验,这些研究关注长新冠中的免疫失调、炎症生物标志物、补体通路及靶向治疗。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 持续升高的促炎细胞因子(包括白细胞介素-6、白细胞介素-1β、肿瘤坏死因子-α、干扰素-γ及白细胞介素-17)与替代途径及凝集素途径的补体激活共同导致内皮损伤、微血管血栓形成、神经炎症、纤维化及多系统功能障碍。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 仍需开展大规模前瞻性研究及随机对照临床试验以验证这些策略并优化长期临床结局。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 新兴生物标志物包括炎症细胞因子、补体蛋白、内皮激活标志物、凝血指标及多组学特征,这些可能有助于疾病分层及治疗监测。整合验证的生物标志物与精准免疫治疗策略可能改善诊断、风险分层及个体化管理。

title: US Public School Operations During the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Scoping Review.
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic forced the sudden closure of schools and a transition to remote learning across the United States. The suspension of in-person education not only altered the delivery of education for millions of students, but it effectively separated many students from vital services and functions that supported their ability to learn and develop. Given the unique role that schools play in educating children and young adults, as well as providing important nonacademic services, their closures led to disruptions in learning, added familial responsibilities, and reduced access to critical social services for students. The reopening of schools for in-person learning or the continuation of remote learning during a public health emergency requires careful planning and consideration to not only ensure the health and safety of students and staff, but also ensure equitable continuation of education and access to nonacademic services. We conducted a scoping review to identify and characterize the literature related to the implementation and impact of interventions and policies used to operate K-12 public schools in the United States during the first 2 years of the COVID-19 pandemic. Through thematic analysis, we found that masking, ventilation, physical distancing, testing, contact tracing, quarantine and isolation, and vaccination interventions allowed schools to safely conduct in-person learning during the pandemic. Findings from the literature suggest that there are suitable mitigation measures that allowed for the safe operation of public schools during the COVID-19 pandemic. The effective implementation of these measures required adequate resources, leadership commitment, and community buy-in.

analysis.summary_en: This scoping review examines how US K-12 public schools were operated during the first two years of the SARS-CoV-2/COVID-19 pandemic, a period that began with sudden closures and a shift to remote learning that disrupted education and access to nonacademic services. Through thematic analysis of the literature on interventions and policies, the authors identified that masking, ventilation, physical distancing, testing, contact tracing, quarantine and isolation, and vaccination enabled schools to safely conduct in-person learning, demonstrating that suitable mitigation measures permitted continued public school operation. The review emphasizes that effective implementation of these measures depended on adequate resources, leadership commitment, and community buy-in, and it underscores the need for careful planning to balance health and safety with equitable educational continuity and access to nonacademic services during future public health emergencies. No specific evidence gaps, controversies or quantitative pooled estimates are reported in the supplied evidence.

title: The influence of hypoxia in predicting COVID-19 mortality in patients with kidney dysfunction on admission in 2 centers in sub-Saharan Africa.
abstract: Kidney dysfunction (KD) and hypoxia on admission are separately associated with COVID-19 mortality. Estimation of GFR using creatinine and peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO2) may be useful for stratification of at-risk populations. We performed a two centers retrospective cohort study of 359 COVID-19 patients aged 18 years or older to explore the impact of admission kidney function and hypoxia in predicting COVID-19 mortality. KD at admission was defined as estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) calculated by CKD EPI < 60 mL /min/1.73 m2 using creatinine and hypoxia as a SpO2 ˂ 90%. Survival (time-to death) curves were built using the Kaplan-Meier methods. Association between mortality, hypoxia and KD was evaluated by multivariate Cox regression models with a significance level of the p-value set at 0.05. There were 152 patients (42.3%) with an eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m2 and 208 patients (74.8%) with hypoxia on admission. Overall in-hospital mortality was 27.6%, rising to 59.7% in patients with eGFR below 60 mL/min and hypoxia (p < 0.001). Survival was lower in the group of patients with a eGFR below 60 mL/min/1.73 m2 and hypoxia (p < 0.001). Predictors of mortality were eGFR ≥ 60 mL/min/1.73 m2 with hypoxia (HR 2.05 [1.01-4.16], p = 0.048), eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m2 without hypoxia (HR 3.20 [1.73-5.94], p < 0.001) and eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m2 with hypoxia (HR 6.55 [3.63-11.84], p < 0.001). KD on admission and hypoxia are common in COVID-19. Its association with in-hospital mortality should encourage its use in the stratification of patients at risk of death. Influence of hypoxia could suggest a pattern of kidney-lung cross talk.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the influence of hypoxia on predicting COVID-19 mortality in patients with kidney dysfunction upon admission, highlighting the need to understand how these factors interact in disease progression.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the influence of hypoxia on predicting COVID-19 mortality in patients with kidney dysfunction upon admission in two centers in sub-Saharan Africa. It found that overall in-hospital mortality was 27.6%, rising to 59.7% in patients with both kidney dysfunction and hypoxia. The results suggest a potential pattern of kidney-lung cross talk, highlighting the importance of incorporating these factors into patient stratification strategies for improved risk assessment and management. The study's retrospective design and potential for confounding factors limit its evidence strength, although the observed statistical associations are robust.

title: Immunological imprinting shapes the cross-reactive antibody responses to the KP.2 and LP.8.1 vaccine doses.
abstract: UNLABELLED: The emergence of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron BA.2.86 subvariant, a lineage derived from the BA.2 strain, led to the 2024-2025 COVID-19 vaccine update to include KP.2 or related JN.1-lineage spike antigens. We evaluated the magnitude, breadth, and durability of humoral immune responses following a single KP.2 vaccine dose in a longitudinal cohort of 21 individuals up to 6 months. KP.2 vaccination increased spike-specific binding and neutralizing antibodies against the ancestral WA.1 strain, as well as against the BA.5, XBB.1.5, and KP.2 variants. Power-law modeling estimated half-lives for WA.1- and KP.2-specific IgG responses at 770 and 248 days, respectively. Additionally, the KP.2 dose increased IgG1 and IgG4 subclasses more than IgG2 and IgG3 responses to both spike proteins. Serum-depletion experiments using WA.1 or KP.2 proteins demonstrated that most vaccine-elicited antibodies were cross-reactive. Consequently, KP.2 vaccine-induced antibodies retained broad neutralizing activity against recently circulating Omicron subvariants (BA.2.86, KP.3.1.1, XEC, LP.8.1, LF.7, XFG.3.12, PQ.1, BA.3.2.1, and RE.2). Using a live virus neutralization assay, XFG.3.12 showed the greatest reduction in neutralizing titers relative to KP.2 (4.2-fold). In a small subset, an LP.8.1 vaccine dose increased neutralizing activity against the matched variant while maintaining WA.1 and KP.2 cross-reactivity, but only modestly increased antibodies to divergent variants BA.3.2.1 and RE.2. Ultimately, these data indicate the KP.2 mRNA vaccine generates durable, cross-reactive responses against current Omicron subvariants. However, ongoing spike evolution impacts the neutralization of emerging lineages, highlighting the need for continued viral monitoring and timely vaccine updates. IMPORTANCE: SARS-CoV-2 continues to evolve, raising ongoing concerns about how well updated vaccines protect against emerging variants. This study evaluates antibody responses after a KP.2 spike mRNA vaccine dose. It shows that a single dose induces durable and broadly cross-reactive immunity against both earlier strains and recently circulating Omicron subvariants. Despite this breadth, reduced neutralizing activity against certain emerging variants indicates that ongoing antigenic changes can impact vaccine-induced antibody effectiveness. These findings provide insight into how current vaccines perform over time and highlight the need to track viral evolution and update vaccine antigens to maintain broad protection against severe disease, hospitalization, and death.

title_zh: 免疫印迹塑造了对KP.2和LP.8.1 疫苗剂量的交叉反应性抗体应答。
source_body_en: UNLABELLED: The emergence of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron BA.2.86 subvariant, a lineage derived from the BA.2 strain, led to the 2024-2025 COVID-19 vaccine update to include KP.2 or related JN.1-lineage spike antigens. We evaluated the magnitude, breadth, and durability of humoral immune responses following a single KP.2 vaccine dose in a longitudinal cohort of 21 individuals up to 6 months. KP.2 vaccination increased spike-specific binding and neutralizing antibodies against the ancestral WA.1 strain, as well as against the BA.5, XBB.1.5, and KP.2 variants. Power-law modeling estimated half-lives for WA.1- and KP.2-specific IgG responses at 770 and 248 days, respectively. Additionally, the KP.2 dose increased IgG1 and IgG4 subclasses more than IgG2 and IgG3 responses to both spike proteins. Serum-depletion experiments using WA.1 or KP.2 proteins demonstrated that most vaccine-elicited antibodies were cross-reactive. Consequently, KP.2 vaccine-induced antibodies retained broad neutralizing activity against recently circulating Omicron subvariants (BA.2.86, KP.3.1.1, XEC, LP.8.1, LF.7, XFG.3.12, PQ.1, BA.3.2.1, and RE.2). Using a live virus neutralization assay, XFG.3.12 showed the greatest reduction in neutralizing titers relative to KP.2 (4.2-fold). In a small subset, an LP.8.1 vaccine dose increased neutralizing activity against the matched variant while maintaining WA.1 and KP.2 cross-reactivity, but only modestly increased antibodies to divergent variants BA.3.2.1 and RE.2. Ultimately, these data indicate the KP.2 mRNA vaccine generates durable, cross-reactive responses against current Omicron subvariants. However, ongoing spike evolution impacts the neutralization of emerging lineages, highlighting the need for continued viral monitoring and timely vaccine updates. IMPORTANCE: SARS-CoV-2 continues to evolve, raising ongoing concerns about how well updated vaccines protect against emerging variants. This study evaluates antibody responses after a KP.2 spike mRNA vaccine dose. It shows that a single dose induces durable and broadly cross-reactive immunity against both earlier strains and recently circulating Omicron subvariants. Despite this breadth, reduced neutralizing activity against certain emerging variants indicates that ongoing antigenic changes can impact vaccine-induced antibody effectiveness. These findings provide insight into how current vaccines perform over time and highlight the need to track viral evolution and update vaccine antigens to maintain broad protection against severe disease, hospitalization, and death.

title: Extracellular vesicles in COVID-19 and long COVID: Structural mediators of viral persistence and immune dysfunction.
abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) have emerged as pivotal structural mediators of immune dysregulation and viral antigen persistence in long COVID. Rather than passive biological carriers, EVs released during SARS-CoV-2 infection function as highly organized lipid nanostructures that preserve the native conformational integrity of viral proteins, including the spike glycoprotein, thereby facilitating chronic signaling and systemic inflammation. Recent advancements in single-particle analytical techniques, such as cryo-electron tomography and atomic force microscopy, are now overcoming the limitations of bulk analysis, enabling the visualization of EV heterogeneity and the quantitative profiling of their nanomechanical properties. This review synthesizes current insights into how EV-associated viral remnants and host-derived inflammatory cargo propagate neuro-immune crosstalk and vascular injury. We conclude by evaluating the potential of EVs as precision biomarkers and bioengineered therapeutic platforms, emphasizing the need for standardized structural characterization to transition these nanovesicles from physiological mediators to clinical diagnostic and regenerative tools.

title: Preliminary miRNA profiling of plasma from patients infected with distinct SARS-CoV-2 variants
abstract: BACKGROUND: Epigenetic regulation can play a dual role in viral infection, acting as part of the host defense, while being hijacked to control viral latency, replication, and persistence. During the COVID-19 pandemic, substantial evidence indicated that different SARS-CoV-2 variants may lead to distinct outcomes by affecting different molecular pathways, including epigenetic mechanisms. METHODS AND RESULTS: In this study, we assessed miRNA expression using high-throughput microarray technology to simultaneously measure the expression of thousands of miRNAs. We focused on: comparing Delta and Omicron infections with healthy controls; identifying specific miRNAs linked to symptom severity; analyzing miRNA expression across different stages of Delta variant infection; and predicting miRNA target genes and evaluating miRNA-mRNA interactions. We identified 65 miRNAs that were significantly differentially expressed simultaneously in both SARS-CoV-2 variants compared to healthy samples. These miRNAs were categorized into distinct functional groups based on their roles in viral infection. We observed an association between the expression of specific miRNAs and virus-induced symptom severity and patients' outcomes in both variants. Furthermore, we examined miRNA expression across the various phases of the Delta variant and identified 38 miRNAs that were significantly differentially expressed. Finally, mRNA-miRNA interaction analysis revealed PTEN, IGF1R, MYC, and STAT3 as the most interacting genes. CONCLUSION: Profiling thousands of miRNAs in response to different SARS-CoV-2 variants offers new opportunities for diagnosis, prognosis, and therapy. Although comorbidities and pathway cross-talk may influence the obtained results, our findings provide novel insights into the host response to SARS-CoV-2 infection at the epigenetic level.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore the role of miRNA in the host response to SARS-CoV-2 variants, particularly focusing on how different variants may affect molecular pathways, including epigenetic mechanisms.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used high-throughput microarray technology to assess miRNA expression in plasma samples from patients infected with distinct SARS-CoV-2 variants, including Delta and Omicron, compared to healthy controls.
analysis.methods: The researchers employed high-throughput microarray technology to measure miRNA expression levels and analyzed miRNA-mRNA interactions to identify potential target genes.
analysis.main_results: The study identified 65 miRNAs that were significantly differentially expressed in both SARS-CoV-2 variants compared to healthy samples, and observed an association between specific miRNA expression and symptom severity in patients.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that miRNA profiling could provide novel insights into the host's epigenetic response to SARS-CoV-2 infection, highlighting potential biomarkers for disease progression.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results may inform the development of diagnostic tools and therapeutic strategies targeting miRNA pathways in SARS-CoV-2 infections, offering potential for improved prognosis and treatment.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on miRNA expression without detailed analysis of comorbidities or pathway cross-talk, and the evidence is based on a single study with a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated miRNA expression in plasma from patients infected with distinct SARS-CoV-2 variants, including Delta and Omicron, compared to healthy controls. Using high-throughput microarray technology, the researchers identified 65 miRNAs that were differentially expressed in both variants and observed an association between specific miRNA expression and symptom severity. The findings suggest that miRNA profiling could offer new insights into the host's epigenetic response to SARS-CoV-2 infection, potentially aiding in diagnosis and treatment. However, the study's results are limited by the absence of detailed analysis of comorbidities and pathway interactions, and the evidence is considered moderate in strength.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在探索微小RNA(miRNA)在宿主宿主对严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2变异株的应答中的作用,重点关注不同变异株如何影响分子通路,包括表观遗传机制。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究采用高通量微阵列技术,评估了感染不同严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2变异株(包括Delta和Omicron)的患者血浆样本中的miRNA表达,并与健康对照组进行了比较。
elements_zh.methods: 研究团队采用高通量微阵列技术测量miRNA表达水平,并通过miRNA-mRNA相互作用分析识别潜在靶基因。
elements_zh.main_results: 该研究在健康样本对比中,识别出65个在严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2两种变异株中显著差异表达的miRNA,并观察到特定miRNA表达与患者症状严重程度之间存在关联。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,miRNA谱分析可能为宿主对严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2感染的表观遗传学反应提供新的见解,并突出潜在的疾病进展生物标志物。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果可能为开发针对严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2感染中miRNA通路的诊断工具和治疗策略提供参考,包括使用抗病毒药物,为改善预后和治疗带来潜在可能。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅关注miRNA表达谱,未深入分析合并症或通路间交叉影响,且基于单项研究,证据强度为中等。

title: Changes in patient conceptualization of asthma and asthma self-management at key timepoints across the COVID-19 pandemic: A qualitative study.
abstract: Abstract Background The COVID‐19 public health emergency had significant impacts on people living with long‐term health conditions. The specific impacts of COVID‐19 on people with asthma across key stages of the pandemic are less certain. This study therefore aimed to explore the experiences of people with asthma across the pandemic as risk levels changed in a retrospective cross‐sectional study. Methods Semi‐structured interviews (N = 20), conducted at one timepoint, asked about experiences covering pre‐COVID, initial outbreak/lockdown, restrictions lifting, key‐stages salient to them (e.g., vaccination) and longer‐term. Data were analysed using thematic‐analysis. Findings There were three themes. ‘Doing my own risk assessment’ was an active process using pre‐existing/acquired knowledge to determine risk and subsequent asthma‐management/COVID‐19 behaviours at all stages. ‘Asthma from background to foreground’ highlighted how asthma that was mostly previously unobtrusive was suddenly a ‘pre‐existing condition’ leading to prolonged stress and anxiety. ‘Place in society’ describes how the participants were included/excluded by society due to safety concerns from the initial outbreak onwards, which was influenced by government, friends, family and neighbours, the media, health care systems and even themselves. Discussion Findings highlight how some people with asthma experienced the pandemic as a threat to mortality, with evidence of both poor and good adjustment to their asthma management, as per the Transdiagnostic model. When there are future rapid changes in contexts affecting long term conditions, government agencies should use the present study's findings to (a) guide decision‐making, (b) inform public health messaging aimed at targeting at‐risk populations and (c) provide support for at‐risk populations.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore how people with asthma conceptualized their condition and self-managed it during key stages of the COVID-19 pandemic, as the specific impacts of the pandemic on asthma patients were less certain.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study was a retrospective cross-sectional qualitative study involving 20 participants with asthma, examining their experiences across pre-COVID, initial outbreak/lockdown, restrictions lifting, and key stages relevant to them, such as vaccination.
analysis.methods: Semi-structured interviews were conducted at one timepoint, and data were analysed using thematic analysis to identify patterns in participants' experiences and conceptualizations of asthma and self-management during the pandemic.
analysis.main_results: Three themes emerged: 'Doing my own risk assessment,' 'Asthma from background to foreground,' and 'Place in society,' highlighting participants' active risk evaluation, heightened awareness of asthma as a pre-existing condition, and societal inclusion/exclusion based on safety concerns.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that the pandemic significantly altered how asthma was perceived and managed, with participants adjusting their behaviors based on evolving risk assessments, as per the Transdiagnostic model.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings can inform public health messaging and support systems for individuals with asthma during future public health emergencies, helping to address their unique needs and concerns.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its single timepoint data collection and reliance on self-reported experiences, which may introduce bias. However, the evidence is strong given the thematic analysis of a representative sample of asthma patients.

analysis.summary_en: This qualitative study investigated how people with asthma conceptualized their condition and managed it during key stages of the COVID-19 pandemic. The research aimed to understand the impact of the pandemic on asthma patients, as the specific effects were uncertain. Using semi-structured interviews with 20 participants, the study identified three themes: active risk assessment, asthma becoming a more prominent concern, and societal inclusion/exclusion based on safety perceptions. The findings highlight how the pandemic influenced asthma management behaviors and mental health, aligning with the Transdiagnostic model. These insights can guide public health strategies for supporting asthma patients during future crises. However, the study's reliance on self-reported data and single timepoint collection may limit the generalizability of the results. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these limitations.

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,疫情显著改变了哮喘的认知与管理方式,参与者基于风险评估动态调整行为,符合跨诊断模型。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 本研究发现可为未来公共卫生紧急事件中哮喘患者的公共卫生信息传播与支持体系提供参考,以满足其特殊需求与关切。

analysis_zh.main_results: 共提炼出三个主题:‘进行自身风险评估’、‘哮喘从背景转为前景’及‘在社会中的位置’。前者体现参与者主动评估风险的过程;第二个主题凸显哮喘作为‘既往存在疾病’的突出感知及随之而来的压力与焦虑;第三个主题描述参与者因安全考量在社会中的接纳或排斥体验。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,疫情显著改变了哮喘的认知与管理方式,参与者基于风险评估动态调整行为,符合跨诊断模型。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 本研究发现可为未来公共卫生紧急事件中哮喘患者的公共卫生信息传播与支持体系提供参考,以满足其特殊需求与关切。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究受限于单一时间点的数据收集及对参与者主观体验的依赖,可能引入偏倚。然而,基于代表性哮喘患者样本的主题分析,证据强度较高。

title: Refining the role of behavioural and social sciences in pandemic response post-COVID-19.
abstract: With the acute stage of COVID-19 behind us, reflection can inform future preparedness. During the pandemic, behavioural and social sciences often studied human behaviour through the lens of alignment with public health recommendations, implicitly treating concern and compliance as desirable and rational. While understandable, this emphasis was relatively narrow. Uncertainty, uneven risk distribution and competing values could have led to heterogeneous appraisals of risk and intervention benefit, even with the evidence available at the time. We show that engaging with the possibility that people could have been heterogeneously rational can broaden understanding of behaviour during COVID-19. Our aim is not to revisit the legitimacy of the response but to encourage reflection on the role of behavioural and social sciences in knowledge generation and highlight opportunities to examine pandemic salience and risk calibration. We outline research directions to guide the field and strengthen decision-making, trust and adaptability in future crises, promoting short-term compliance and long-term trust.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the role of behavioural and social sciences in pandemic response, specifically examining how these disciplines have studied human behaviour during the COVID-19 pandemic. The central question is about the breadth and depth of this role, particularly in understanding the variability of human responses to public health interventions. The topic boundary includes SARS-CoV-2, its variants, and related terms such as 'post-COVID condition' and 'long COVID'.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of existing literature, with no explicit mention of systematic review methods or meta-analysis. It draws on general observations and interpretations of studies conducted during the pandemic, focusing on the conceptual frameworks used to understand human behaviour. The review does not report specific databases, search dates, or eligibility criteria.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review highlights that the focus on aligning human behaviour with public health recommendations during the pandemic was relatively narrow. It suggests that this approach may have overlooked the complexity of human decision-making, particularly in the context of uncertainty and varying risk perceptions. The authors argue that considering heterogeneous rationality among individuals can enhance understanding of pandemic-related behaviours.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that the narrow focus on compliance with public health recommendations may have led to an oversimplified view of human behaviour. It also identifies a gap in understanding how people perceive and calibrate risks during pandemics, especially in the context of uncertainty and uneven risk distribution. These limitations suggest a need for more nuanced approaches in future research.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review recommends expanding the scope of behavioural and social science research to include a broader range of human responses and decision-making processes. It emphasizes the importance of examining pandemic salience and risk calibration to improve future preparedness, decision-making, and trust in public health measures.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the role of behavioural and social sciences in pandemic response, particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic. It critiques the narrow focus on aligning human behaviour with public health recommendations and highlights the need for a more comprehensive understanding of risk perception and decision-making. The authors suggest that considering heterogeneous rationality among individuals can improve pandemic preparedness and response. They also identify gaps in current research and recommend future directions to enhance trust and adaptability in public health strategies.
