title: Factors associated with vaccination against Seasonal Influenza and SARS-CoV-2 in the UK among FluSurvey participants, 2023-2025.
abstract: Seasonal Influenza and COVID-19 vaccination programmes are critical for reducing morbidity and mortality in older adults, yet uptake remains uneven across populations. We aimed to profile vaccination attitudes and examine predictors of COVID-19/influenza vaccination uptake among a UK participatory surveillance system - FluSurvey. We analysed FluSurvey data from participants aged [≥]65 years who were eligible for both vaccines in the 2023-2024 and 2024-2025 Autumn - Winter seasonal campaigns. Descriptive analyses examined self-reported attitudes to influenza vaccination. Logistic regression examined factors (age, sex, socioeconomic status, education, employment, transport, smoking and chronic conditions) associated with influenza and COVID-19 vaccination uptake in each season, adjusting for confounders. Belonging to a risk group and reducing risk of influenza were frequently reported motivations for influenza vaccination, while building natural immunity and concerns around safety and adverse effects were frequently reported barriers. Individuals vaccinated against COVID-19 were more likely to receive an influenza vaccination (aOR2023-2024=13.90 [9.28-21.17]; aOR2024-2025=8.54 [5.82-12.60]), and vice-versa (aOR2023-2024=13.91 [9.30-21.19]; aOR2024-2025=8.52 [5.81-12.58]). Lower educational attainment was associated with lower odds of COVID-19 vaccination (aOR2023-2024=0.59 [0.45-0.78], aOR2024-2025: 0.56 [0.39-0.79]). Other results were weaker or demonstrated variation by season. Our findings highlight recent attitudes and barriers to influenza and COVID-19 vaccination among the FluSurvey cohort, which may inform approaches to improve vaccination coverage in the population.

title_zh: 2023-2025年英国FluSurvey参与者中与疫苗接种季节性流感及严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2相关的因素
source_body_en: Seasonal Influenza and COVID-19 vaccination programmes are critical for reducing morbidity and mortality in older adults, yet uptake remains uneven across populations. We aimed to profile vaccination attitudes and examine predictors of COVID-19/influenza vaccination uptake among a UK participatory surveillance system - FluSurvey. We analysed FluSurvey data from participants aged [≥]65 years who were eligible for both vaccines in the 2023-2024 and 2024-2025 Autumn - Winter seasonal campaigns. Descriptive analyses examined self-reported attitudes to influenza vaccination. Logistic regression examined factors (age, sex, socioeconomic status, education, employment, transport, smoking and chronic conditions) associated with influenza and COVID-19 vaccination uptake in each season, adjusting for confounders. Belonging to a risk group and reducing risk of influenza were frequently reported motivations for influenza vaccination, while building natural immunity and concerns around safety and adverse effects were frequently reported barriers. Individuals vaccinated against COVID-19 were more likely to receive an influenza vaccination (aOR2023-2024=13.90 [9.28-21.17]; aOR2024-2025=8.54 [5.82-12.60]), and vice-versa (aOR2023-2024=13.91 [9.30-21.19]; aOR2024-2025=8.52 [5.81-12.58]). Lower educational attainment was associated with lower odds of COVID-19 vaccination (aOR2023-2024=0.59 [0.45-0.78], aOR2024-2025: 0.56 [0.39-0.79]). Other results were weaker or demonstrated variation by season. Our findings highlight recent attitudes and barriers to influenza and COVID-19 vaccination among the FluSurvey cohort, which may inform approaches to improve vaccination coverage in the population.

title: Estimation of serial intervals and time-varying reproduction numbers across SARS-CoV-2 variants in childcare clusters: symptom onset vs. reporting dates
abstract: Abstract Background Respiratory virus transmission in childcare centers is facilitated by dense contact patterns, making accurate estimation of serial intervals (SI) and time-varying reproduction numbers (Rt) essential for outbreak management. Although symptom onset dates are epidemiologically preferred, reporting dates are frequently used in routine surveillance due to operational constraints. Reliance on reporting dates may introduce systematic bias in transmission parameter estimates. This study aimed to evaluate differences in SI and Rt estimates based on symptom onset versus reporting dates in COVID-19 childcare clusters across SARS-CoV-2 variant periods. Methods Nationwide data from the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency (January 2020–February 2022) were analyzed. Four genotype-confirmed clusters meeting the predefined eligibility criteria were included: one Before Delta, two Delta, and one Omicron cluster, each comprising at least 50 epidemiologically linked cases. Serial intervals were fitted using gamma distributions. Time-varying Rt values were estimated using the EpiEstim package separately based on symptom onset and reporting dates. Results Onset-based mean SI declined from 9.85 days (95% CI: 1.97–23.95) in the Before Delta period to 5.34 days (95% CI: 2.00–10.28) during Omicron. In contrast, reporting-based SI estimates were generally longer, reaching 8.87 days (95% CI: 0.71–27.08) during Omicron. Across all variant periods, reporting-based Rt estimates were consistently lower than onset-based estimates. For example, during the Delta period, mean Rt was 1.90 (95% CI: 0.79–3.76) using onset dates compared with 1.08 (95% CI: 0.41–2.39) using reporting dates. Conclusion The choice of temporal reference substantially affects SI and Rt estimation in childcare clusters. Reliance on reporting dates may underestimate real-time transmission intensity and distort epidemic risk assessment. Prioritizing symptom onset data in surveillance systems may improve the accuracy and timeliness of public health responses in high-risk settings.

Prioritizing symptom onset data in surveillance systems may improve the accuracy and timeliness of public health responses in high-risk settings.

title: Prognostic impact of right ventricular dilatation and echocardiography use criteria in hospitalized COVID-19 patients.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The surge of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 [coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19)] infection created unprecedented diagnostic and logistical pressures. Given the established potential for cardiac injury and the critical need to optimize scarce resources, establishing the clinical utility and prognostic value of transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) became imperative. AIM: To evaluate the prognostic predictors and the adherence to appropriate use criteria (AUC) for TTE in a highly affected setting. title: Inequalities in mortality following SARS-CoV-2 infection for people with severe mental illness during and following vaccination roll-out in England: a retrospective, whole-country linked cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: People with severe mental illness (SMI) had a higher risk of death following SARS-CoV-2 infection compared with people without SMI during the COVID-19 pandemic peak. It is unclear whether this risk reduced in later stages after vaccination roll-out. We aimed to assess all-cause and cause-specific mortality following SARS-CoV-2 infection in people with or without SMI across pandemic stages, using whole-country data, while accounting for sociodemographic and clinical characteristics. METHODS: In this retrospective, whole-country cohort study, we analysed linked electronic health records for all people in England registered to primary care who were alive in November, 2019 (>99% of the population). The study population included people who had COVID-19 between Jan 31, 2020, and June 30, 2023, with information on deaths and vaccination. Data extracted from the NHS England Secure Data Environment provided through the British Heart Foundation Data Science Centre CVD-COVID-UK-COVID-IMPACT Consortium linked datasets were curated to form a dataset in July, 2024. Cox regression estimated differences in all-cause and COVID-19 mortality. Analyses were stratified by pandemic stages, defined by WHO policy and UK Government vaccination roll-out: Jan 31-Sept 30, 2020 (stage 1); Oct 1, 2020-July 18, 2021 (stage 2, vaccination roll-out); and July 19, 2021-June 30, 2023 (stage 3, post-vaccination roll-out). SMI comprised schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, bipolar disorder, or other affective and non-affective disorder with psychosis. A patient and public involvement panel was consulted during design phases of the study. FINDINGS: 13 463 945 people with COVID-19 were identified, of whom 160 190 (1·19%) had SMI. People with SMI were older [mean age [SD], SMI 49·7 years [17·9], non-SMI 45·0 years [17·6]), had a similar sex split (females SMI vs non-SMI: 56·3% vs 56·6%); and were mostly White British (77·3% or 76·3%). People with SMI had higher all-cause mortality than those without (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 1·56, 95% CI 1·53-1·59). All-cause mortality risk in people with SMI was elevated in stage 1 (aHR 1·27, 95% CI 1·22-1·32), but larger in the stage 2 (aHR 1·56, 1·51-1·61) and stage 3 (aHR 1·55, 1·50-1·59). Vaccination prevalence was initially higher for people with SMI (in stage 2: 112 795 [73·2%, 95% CI 72·9-73·4], compared with people without SMI, 8 852 970 [67·4%, 67·3-67·4]). By study end, fewer people with SMI were fully vaccinated (127 145 [79·4%, 79·2-79·6]), compared with people without SMI (11 605 915 [87·2%, 87·2-87·3]. Higher COVID-19 mortality risk in people with SMI persisted but was partially attenuated by vaccination (aHR 1·25, 1·17-1·34). INTERPRETATION: Excess mortality in people with SMI persisted throughout the COVID-19 pandemic. Preventive public health and clinical strategies are needed to address excess mortality and lower vaccination. FUNDING: Health Foundation-Academy of Medical Sciences.

title: Sources of Stress in Relation to Sleep Health During the COVID-19 Pandemic: Findings from the National Couples' Health and Time Study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE To assess associations between sources of stress and sleep health among married/cohabitating US adults during the COVID-19 pandemic. METHODS We analyzed the National Couples' Health and Time Study, an online survey completed 2020-2021. Stressors were categorized into five domains--1) COVID-19 infection; 2) resources/insurance; 3) overall health; 4) job/income; and 5) public health recommendations. Sleep quality and duration (<7 and 7-9) were measured. Adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) and Accepted manuscript ACCEPTED MANUSCRIPT95% CIs were obtained from survey-weighted logistic regression models by estimating predicted marginal probabilities. RESULTS Among 3,642 individuals, 46.6% were aged 35-50 years and 44.1% were college graduates. Within racial and/or ethnic groups, the weighted prevalence of overall health stress was 62.0% among Latino and 55.8% among White individuals; the weighted prevalence of job/income stress was 64.3% among Black/African American and 57.6% among White individuals; and the weighted prevalence of public health recommendations stress was highest among White individuals (34.1%), compared with Black/African American (28.1%) and Latino (27.8%) individuals. Overall health stress was associated with poor/fair sleep quality (aPR=1.35; 95% CI: 1.14-1.60) and <7 hours sleep (aPR=1.19; 95% CI: 1.03-1.39). Job/income stress was associated with fair/poor sleep quality (aPR=1.46; 95% CI: 1.24-1.72) and <7 hours sleep (aPR=1.31; 95% CI: 1.13-1.52). Race-stratified models showed job/income stress significant among Latino and White individuals for both sleep outcomes, and overall health stress among Latino individuals for duration. CONCLUSION Overall health stress and job/income stress were associated with poorer sleep health among married and cohabiting individuals. Futurework is needed on stress-management and sleep health promotion.

source_records.title: Sources of Stress in Relation to Sleep Health During the COVID-19 Pandemic: Findings from the National Couples' Health and Time Study.
source_records.abstract: OBJECTIVE To assess associations between sources of stress and sleep health among married/cohabitating US adults during the COVID-19 pandemic. METHODS We analyzed the National Couples' Health and Time Study, an online survey completed 2020-2021. Stressors were categorized into five domains--1) COVID-19 infection; 2) resources/insurance; 3) overall health; 4) job/income; and 5) public health recommendations. Sleep quality and duration (<7 and 7-9) were measured. Adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) and Accepted manuscript ACCEPTED MANUSCRIPT95% CIs were obtained from survey-weighted logistic regression models by estimating predicted marginal probabilities. RESULTS Among 3,642 individuals, 46.6% were aged 35-50 years and 44.1% were college graduates. Within racial and/or ethnic groups, the weighted prevalence of overall health stress was 62.0% among Latino and 55.8% among White individuals; the weighted prevalence of job/income stress was 64.3% among Black/African American and 57.6% among White individuals; and the weighted prevalence of public health recommendations stress was highest among White individuals (34.1%), compared with Black/African American (28.1%) and Latino (27.8%) individuals. Overall health stress was associated with poor/fair sleep quality (aPR=1.35; 95% CI: 1.14-1.60) and <7 hours sleep (aPR=1.19; 95% CI: 1.03-1.39). Job/income stress was associated with fair/poor sleep quality (aPR=1.46; 95% CI: 1.24-1.72) and <7 hours sleep (aPR=1.31; 95% CI: 1.13-1.52). Race-stratified models showed job/income stress significant among Latino and White individuals for both sleep outcomes, and overall health stress among Latino individuals for duration. CONCLUSION Overall health stress and job/income stress were associated with poorer sleep health among married and cohabiting individuals. Futurework is needed on stress-management and sleep health promotion.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the associations between sources of stress and sleep health among married and cohabitating US adults during the COVID-19 pandemic. Using data from the National Couples' Health and Time Study, stressors were categorized into five domains, including overall health, job/income, and public health recommendations. Sleep quality and duration were measured, and adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using survey-weighted logistic regression models. However, the study's reliance on self-reported data and its focus on a specific population limit the generalizability of the findings, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

title: African Americans' perspective on COVID-19 and influenza vaccines: A qualitative study.
abstract: Purpose Annual vaccinations, such as influenza and COVID-19, are a safe and effective way of preventing disease and promoting healthier communities, yet many factors impact uptake. Black and African Americans face numerous barriers to vaccination, reflected in consistently lower vaccination rates and higher hospitalization and mortality rates. This qualitative study aimed to understand perceptions and factors influencing COVID-19 and influenza vaccination among Black and African American adults to inform interventions and outreach to prevent increased acuity of vaccination disparities. Eighty-six Black and African Americans in Milwaukee, WI were purposively recruited to participate in in-depth interviews. Major Findings We identified two themes and five subthemes reflecting vaccine perspectives, influences, and decision-making. In the first theme, similarities and differences in attitudes and willingness to get vaccinated against influenza and COVID-19, we identified three subthemes: (1) prevention was a motivating factor for getting both COVID-19 and influenza vaccines; (2) mistrust surrounding COVID-19 and the COVID-19 vaccine fueled hesitancy; and (3) some participants held discordant beliefs surrounding vaccines and healthcare. In the second theme, sources of vaccine information influencing vaccine perspectives , we identified two subthemes: (1) main sources of vaccine information were television news and the internet, not trusted healthcare professionals, and (2) life experiences affected perspectives. Conclusions Our findings show that vaccine perspectives are shaped by a complex interplay of personal beliefs, experiences, cultural identity, and trust. Public health strategies to improve vaccination rates should acknowledge mistrust, dispel myths and misinformation, and engage trusted communities and messengers across both healthcare and community settings.

title: Data-Driven Change-Point SEIR Modeling of the 2025 COVID-19 Epidemic Wave in China: Model Comparison, Robustness Analysis, and Residual Diagnostics
abstract: Abstract Background: National COVID-19 surveillance in China showed a pronounced epidemic wave during spring 2025, followed by a sustained decline through the summer. This study examined whether that trajectory could be adequately represented by a standard SEIR model with a constant transmission rate or whether the data supported a structural change in transmission intensity. Methods: We analyzed 153 consecutive days of nationally reported COVID-19 cases from 1 May through 30 September 2025. Daily observations were digitized from official China CDC figures and calibrated to the corresponding monthly totals. A standard susceptible-exposed-infectious-removed (SEIR) model was fitted under two specifications: a constant-beta baseline and a piecewise-beta model with a change point selected by profiling candidate dates and minimizing the Akaike Information Criterion (AIC). The main analysis fixed the latent period at 3 days, the infectious period at 5 days, and used an observation scaling factor q to connect model incidence with reported cases. Model performance was assessed using R-squared, RMSE, AIC, and BIC. Robustness was evaluated through change-point, observation-scale, and biological-parameter sensitivity analyses, followed by residual diagnostics for day-of-week structure and temporal autocorrelation. Results: The AIC profile selected 24 May 2025 as the optimal change point, two days before the observed case peak on 26 May. The piecewise model substantially outperformed the constant-beta model (R-squared 0.8690 vs. 0.6689; RMSE 1,861.07 vs. 2,959.03; AIC 2,313.85 vs. 2,451.74; BIC 2,329.00 vs. The model-implied reproduction index declined from 1.4006 before the change point to 0.8725 afterward. This directional transition from expansion to contraction was preserved across all tested change-point dates, observation-scale values, and nine latent/infectious-period combinations, although goodness of fit deteriorated under some extreme biological assumptions. Residuals retained a strong weekly reporting pattern and positive autocorrelation. Conclusions: A data-driven piecewise transmission rate provided a markedly better description of the 2025 epidemic wave than a constant-rate SEIR model. The strongest inference is a robust structural transition in transmission dynamics in late May rather than a precise estimate of any single biological parameter or a causal attribution to a specific intervention.

title: A Three-Domain Framework for Interpreting Publicly Reported Outbreak Surveillance Data: Illustrative Lessons from COVID-19 Outbreaks in China
abstract: Abstract Background Publicly reported outbreak surveillance data are subject to multiple sources of uncertainty, including variation in case ascertainment, testing protocols, and health-system conditions. Standard epidemiological methods can be applied to assess whether reported figures are internally interpretable under reasonable statistical assumptions. This study uses two COVID-19 outbreaks in China—the 2020 Wuhan epidemic and the 2021 Putian Delta-variant outbreak—as illustrative cases to examine methodological considerations in the analysis of publicly reported outbreak data. Methods Three analytical domains were examined using publicly available data. First, reported case fatality rates (CFRs) from Wuhan and the rest of China were compared to illustrate the effect of differential case ascertainment on regional CFR ratios. Second, the RT-PCR testing sequence of the Putian index case was assessed using a temporal plausibility framework informed by published time-varying sensitivity curves, without formal probability estimation. Third, infection outcomes among two student swab-collector cohorts (Putian, n = 320, 27 days; Tianshui, n = 413, approximately 3 days) were compared using a person-time standardized Poisson incidence density framework, with exact Poisson confidence intervals and incidence rate ratio estimation. Results The Wuhan CFR (7.68%) was 3.47 times the non-Wuhan CFR (2.21%), a difference compatible with multiple explanations including differential ascertainment and health-system conditions. The Putian index case testing sequence was more consistent with late-quarantine infection than with infection present from the date of arrival, though the available data permit multiple interpretations. Person-time standardization materially changed the interpretation of the student cohort comparison: the Putian cohort contributed 8,640 person-days with zero infections (incidence density: 0, 95% CI: 0–0.43 per 1,000 person-days), compared with the Tianshui cohort’s 1,239 person-days with 3 infections (2.42, 95% CI: 0.50–7.07 per 1,000 person-days). The incidence rate ratio was not calculable under a standard Poisson model due to the zero-event numerator; a mid-p exact method yielded an upper bound consistent with a lower observed rate in the Putian cohort under the stated assumptions, although risk homogeneity cannot be verified. Conclusions The analyses illustrate three methodological principles relevant to outbreak surveillance: regional CFR ratios require adjustment for ascertainment conditions before substantive interpretation; RT-PCR sequence assessment benefits from time-varying rather than constant sensitivity assumptions; and person-time standardization is a prerequisite for valid comparison of cohorts with unequal follow-up duration. Access to primary records would be necessary for more definitive epidemiological characterization of the events described.

analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide cautious guidance for interpreting publicly reported outbreak surveillance data, particularly in assessing case fatality rates and infection dynamics in different populations and settings.

analysis.summary_en: This study presents a three-domain framework for interpreting publicly reported outbreak surveillance data, using two illustrative cases of COVID-19 outbreaks in China. The first domain compared case fatality rates (CFRs) between Wuhan and other regions, highlighting the impact of differential case ascertainment. The second domain assessed the RT-PCR testing sequence of the Putian index case using a temporal plausibility framework, suggesting late-quarantine infection. The third domain compared infection outcomes in two student swab-collector cohorts, emphasizing the importance of person-time standardization for valid comparisons. The analyses underscore methodological principles for interpreting outbreak data, including adjustment for ascertainment conditions, use of time-varying sensitivity assumptions, and standardization for cohort comparisons. The study's findings have implications for improving the accuracy and interpretation of surveillance data, but the reliance on abstract-level data and assumptions limits the confidence in the conclusions.

title: Editorial: The influence of SARS-CoV-2 infection and long-COVID on the incidence of viral coinfection
abstract: Abdullah MY (9) studied the impact of COVID-19 on cytokines and gene polymorphisms in patients with type 1 diabetes. Machine learning analyses identified IL-18, CRP, and IL-6 as key biomarkers of COVID-19 severity, with IL-18 being the most important.In long COVID patients, Fricke F et al (10) found downregulation of pro-inflammatory genes in classical monocytes, including IL1β and CXCL2. Their analysis suggested reduced inflammasome activity (via SNAI1) and impaired monocyte differentiation (via ATF2), leading them to conclude that circulating monocytes are either immature or exhausted. analyzed T cell and TCR data from hospitalized Omicron patients and found that a significant proportion of TCRs targeted epitopes across the SARS-CoV-2 genome, including non-structural proteins implicated in viral replication and immune evasion. Their findings highlight how T cell protective immunity is influenced by both the viral replication cycle and HLA type, affecting TCR affinity and clonotype formation. Furthermore, Wen, Y. (12) et al evaluated the heterogeneity and transcriptomic characteristics of Tregs in COVID-19 patients and concluded that Tregs may be activated through the bystander effect, as evidenced by the analysis of TCR clonotype characteristics. The analysis proposed possible analyses of treatment strategies in SARS-CoV-2infected patients.The response against SARS-CoV-2 infection in the elderly population after 6 months was analyzed by Luo Q. The decline in memory B cells and CD69+ and CD38+ T cells, along with the rise in PD-1+ and CTLA-4+ in CD4+/CD8+ T cells and double-negative B cells, suggests that immune responses to BA.5 infection may diminish more quickly in the elderly. (14) developed an explainable machine learning-based mortality risk stratification for older adults with COVID-19, pinpointing core immunological biomarkers and revealing dose-threshold effects. The model identified 10 key features: basophil percentage, C-reactive protein, procalcitonin, D-dimer AST/ALT ratio, cardiac troponin I, standard bicarbonate, age, aspartate transaminase, and oxygen saturation. Those parameters were considered critical for calculating patient survival.Chen L et al. (15) reviewed mitochondrial metabolism in COVID-19, highlighting the need for longterm patient data and addressing analytical limitations. They suggested that nutrients like CoQ10, NAC, and creatine could help restore energy metabolism and reduce oxidative stress. The authors emphasized the importance of interdisciplinary collaboration for multi-omics studies of mitochondrial-epigenetic interactions, targeted antioxidants, and optimized nutrient delivery systems.Marandu et al. (16) found that vaccination benefited patient recovery from viral infections. While CD4 cells were impacted only during active infection, changes in B and NK cells were noted in the vaccinated group. Additionally, T cell hyperresponsiveness was seen in patients with severe disease. Fialho, M.J., and colleagues (17) studied the role of neutralizing antibodies against COVID-19 and its variants. They concluded that while COVID-19 vaccination effectively generates protective immunity, challenges remain due to immune evasion by Omicron subvariants and waning immunity. These findings highlight the need for updated booster strategies and sustained public health efforts for full vaccine coverage and long-term protection.Yin, Z. et al (18) analyzed data from large-scale serosurveys and found that median IgG antibody levels declined after 3 months. Higher levels were linked to prior infection and vaccination, while older age was associated with annual decay, especially in adults ≥60 years. The IgG threshold for protection against XBB reinfection was 400 AU/mL, with each additional vaccination reducing reinfection risk by 13-15%.Bansai A (19) emphasized that no single protein can diagnose post-COVID patients; phenotypelinked multi-analyte panels show the most promise. Effective post-COVID research requires standardized case definitions, cross-platform validation, and the integration of coagulation assays and extracellular vesicle profiling to improve tissue signal detection.Cruz-Altamirano, E et al. (20) conducted a pilot proteomic analysis on immune dysregulation in dengue following prior SARS-CoV-2 infection. They concluded that previous SARS-CoV-2 exposure may increase dengue severity through cross-reactive antibodies, shifting the immune response toward Th2 and enhancing viral replication. Furthermore, Parra-González M. ( 21) and colleagues reviewed the interactions between dengue and SARS-CoV-2 and their impact on clinical outcomes. They found that co-infection may worsen inflammation, increase vascular and organ damage, and complicate treatment. However, definitive evidence for antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE) remains inconclusive, highlighting the need for further mechanistic research.The proteomic profile analysis of hospitalized HIV-and SARS-CoV-2 coinfected patients was studied by Zhang, X. The proteomic profile highlighted disruptions in immunomodulation, thrombosis, and viral entry pathways in people living with HIV caused by COVID-19. However, a larger trial is needed to ascertain the effect of coinfection on immune response.The assessment of Programmed cell death markers in COVID-19 survivors with and without sepsis was analyzed by Mallapu G et al. The analysis revealed two molecular signatures linked to disease severity. The first signature, showing high levels of secreted programmed cell death markers (IL-1-β, IFN-γ, MHC I-A, MHC II-DRB1), was found in both COVID-19-Sepsis and no Sepsis cohorts. The second signature, containing cellular programmed cell death markers (caspase-1, caspase-3, MLKL, p62/SQSTM1), was specific to the COVID-19-Sepsis cohort. These signatures may serve as biomarkers for disease severity and guide therapeutic interventions in critical care.The relationship between SARS-CoV-2 infection and Streptococcus pneumoniae colonization and disease severity was analyzed by Calvo-Silveira, S., et al. Patients with co-infections have higher co-morbidities and severe clinical presentations. Interestingly, non-pharmacological measures may disrupt the S. pneumoniae dynamics, and COVID vaccination can prevent the possibility of coinfection and decrease disease severity.Currey J et al. (25) studied post-viral sequelae using a mouse model of influenza and SARS-CoV-2 in C57BL/6 mice. They infected the mice with sublethal doses of SARS-CoV-2 (MA30) or influenza A (PR8) and analyzed lung and brain tissues at 14-, 21-, and 28-days post-infection using histological analysis and bulk-RNA sequencing. They were able to establish distinct tissue-specific trajectories of long-term pathology following SARS-CoV-2 and influenza infection and provide a foundation for dissecting the mechanisms of post-viral lung and brain disease.The topic presents a compelling collection of manuscripts that cover several critical aspects of SARS-CoV-2 infection, vaccine evaluation, and coinfection, thereby enabling readers to gain a comprehensive understanding of this intricate phenomenon. Notably, there are various proposals for conducting rational risk analyses regarding disease severity, evaluating the immune response to the virus, and assessing the effects of vaccination. Furthermore, suggestions for therapeutic targets that may prove beneficial for future investigations, including those related to long COVID, have been identified. Despite the pandemic originating over six years ago, several unresolved issues persist, particularly regarding post-infection consequences. Consequently, further research is essential to unravel the complex elements associated with infection and coinfection.

Those parameters were considered critical for calculating patient survival.Chen L et al. (15) reviewed mitochondrial metabolism in COVID-19, highlighting the need for longterm patient data and addressing analytical limitations. They suggested that nutrients like CoQ10, NAC, and creatine could help restore energy metabolism and reduce oxidative stress. The authors emphasized the importance of interdisciplinary collaboration for multi-omics studies of mitochondrial-epigenetic interactions, targeted antioxidants, and optimized nutrient delivery systems.Marandu et al. (16) found that vaccination benefited patient recovery from viral infections. While CD4 cells were impacted only during active infection, changes in B and NK cells were noted in the vaccinated group. Additionally, T cell hyperresponsiveness was seen in patients with severe disease. Fialho, M.J., and colleagues (17) studied the role of neutralizing antibodies against COVID-19 and its variants. These signatures may serve as biomarkers for disease severity and guide therapeutic interventions in critical care.The relationship between SARS-CoV-2 infection and Streptococcus pneumoniae colonization and disease severity was analyzed by Calvo-Silveira, S., et al. Patients with co-infections have higher co-morbidities and severe clinical presentations. Interestingly, non-pharmacological measures may disrupt the S. pneumoniae dynamics, and COVID vaccination can prevent the possibility of coinfection and decrease disease severity.Currey J et al. (25) studied post-viral sequelae using a mouse model of influenza and SARS-CoV-2 in C57BL/6 mice. They infected the mice with sublethal doses of SARS-CoV-2 (MA30) or influenza A (PR8) and analyzed lung and brain tissues at 14-, 21-, and 28-days post-infection using histological analysis and bulk-RNA sequencing. They were able to establish distinct tissue-specific trajectories of long-term pathology following SARS-CoV-2 and influenza infection and provide a foundation for dissecting the mechanisms of post-viral lung and brain disease.The topic presents a compelling collection of manuscripts that cover several critical aspects of SARS-CoV-2 infection, vaccine evaluation, and coinfection, thereby enabling readers to gain a comprehensive understanding of this intricate phenomenon. Notably, there are various proposals for conducting rational risk analyses regarding disease severity, evaluating the immune response to the virus, and assessing the effects of vaccination. Furthermore, suggestions for therapeutic targets that may prove beneficial for future investigations, including those related to long COVID, have been identified. Despite the pandemic originating over six years ago, several unresolved issues persist, particularly regarding post-infection consequences. Consequently, further research is essential to unravel the complex elements associated with infection and coinfection.

title_original: Editorial: The influence of SARS-CoV-2 infection and long-COVID on the incidence of viral coinfection

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore how SARS-CoV-2 infection and long-COVID influence the incidence of viral coinfection, highlighting the need to understand the interplay between these conditions and other pathogens.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed T cell and TCR data from hospitalized Omicron patients, focusing on the immune response to SARS-CoV-2 and its variants, including non-structural proteins involved in viral replication and immune evasion.
analysis.methods: Machine learning analyses identified key biomarkers of COVID-19 severity, such as IL-18, CRP, and IL-6, while also examining TCR clonotype characteristics in long COVID patients to assess monocyte function and differentiation.
analysis.main_results: A significant proportion of TCRs targeted epitopes across the SARS-CoV-2 genome, including non-structural proteins, and the analysis suggested reduced inflammasome activity and impaired monocyte differentiation, indicating potential immune exhaustion or immaturity.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the complex relationship between T cell protective immunity, the viral replication cycle, and HLA type, which influence TCR affinity and clonotype formation in SARS-CoV-2 infection.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results suggest that understanding T cell responses and their modulation by viral factors and HLA types could inform strategies for improving immune responses and managing long-term effects of SARS-CoV-2 infection.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on hospitalized Omicron patients and the lack of long-term follow-up data, which may affect the generalizability of the findings. The evidence is moderate due to these constraints.

analysis.summary_en: This editorial explores the influence of SARS-CoV-2 infection and long-COVID on viral coinfection incidence. It highlights the need to understand how these conditions interact with other pathogens and affect immune responses. The study analyzed T cell and TCR data from hospitalized Omicron patients, identifying key biomarkers and suggesting reduced inflammasome activity and impaired monocyte differentiation. These findings emphasize the role of the viral replication cycle and HLA type in shaping TCR affinity and clonotype formation. The results have implications for improving immune responses and managing long-term effects of SARS-CoV-2, though the study's moderate evidence strength is limited by its focus on hospitalized patients and lack of long-term data.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究分析了住院 Omicron 患者的 T 细胞和 TCR 数据,重点关注 免疫应答 对 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 及其变体的影响,包括参与病毒复制和免疫逃逸的非结构蛋白。
elements_zh.methods: Machine learning analyses identified key biomarkers of COVID-19 severity, such as IL-18, CRP, and IL-6, while also examining TCR clonotype characteristics in long COVID patients to assess monocyte function and differentiation.
elements_zh.main_results: 相当比例的 TCR 针对 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 基因组 的表位,包括非结构蛋白;分析提示炎症小体活性下降和单核细胞分化受损,表明可能存在免疫耗竭或未成熟。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果凸显了 T 细胞保护性免疫、病毒复制周期和 HLA 类型之间的复杂关系,这些因素共同影响 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染中的 TCR 亲和力和克隆型形成。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果表明,理解 T 细胞应答及其受病毒因素和 HLA 类型调控的机制,可为改进 免疫应答 并管理 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染的长期影响提供策略指导。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究局限于住院 Omicron 患者,且缺乏长期随访数据,可能影响结果的普适性。鉴于这些限制,证据强度为中等。

(12) 等评估了 新型冠状病毒感染 患者 Tregs 的异质性和转录组特征,得出 Tregs 可能通过旁观者效应被激活的结论,依据是 TCR 克隆型特征的分析。该分析提出在 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染患者中可能的 治疗 策略。Luo Q 对老年人 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染 6 个月后的应答进行分析。记忆 B 细胞以及 CD69+、CD38+ T 细胞下降,同时 CD4+/CD8+ T 细胞和双阴性 B 细胞中 PD-1+、CTLA-4+ 上升,提示老年人对 BA.5 感染的 免疫应答 可能更快减弱。(14) 开发了一种可解释的机器学习基于 死亡率 的老年人风险分层模型,定位核心免疫生物标志物并揭示剂量阈值效应。模型识别出 10 项关键特征:嗜碱细胞比例、C‐反应蛋白、降钙素原、D‐二聚体、AST/ALT 比值、心肌肌钙蛋白 I、标准碳酸氢盐、年龄、天冬氨酸转氨酶和血氧饱和度。这些参数被视为计算患者生存率的关键。Chen L 等 (15) 回顾了 新型冠状病毒感染 中的线粒体代谢,强调需要长期患者数据并指出分析局限性。他们建议 CoQ10、NAC 和肌酸等营养素可帮助恢复能量代谢并降低氧化应激。作者强调跨学科合作在多组学研究线粒体‐表观遗传相互作用、靶向抗氧化剂以及优化营养递送系统中的重要性。Marandu 等 (16) 发现 疫苗接种 有助于患者从病毒感染中恢复。CD4 细胞仅在活动感染期间受影响,疫苗接种组的 B 细胞和 NK 细胞出现变化。此外,重症患者出现 T 细胞过度反应。Fialho,M.J. 等 (17) 研究了针对 新型冠状病毒感染 及其变体的中和抗体作用。他们得出 新型冠状病毒感染 疫苗接种 能有效产生保护性免疫,但因 Omicron 亚变种的免疫逃逸和免疫衰减仍面临挑战。这些发现凸显了更新加强针策略和持续公共卫生努力以实现全面 疫苗 覆盖和长期保护的必要性。Yin,Z. 等 (18) 分析了大规模血清流行调查数据,发现 IgG 中位抗体水平在 3 个月后下降。较高水平与既往感染和 疫苗接种 相关,而年龄增大尤其在 ≥60 岁成人中与年衰减相关。针对 XBB 再感染的 IgG 保护阈值为 400 AU/mL,每增加一次 疫苗接种 可将再感染风险降低 13‐15%。Bansai A (19) 强调单一蛋白无法诊断后 COVID 患者;表型关联的多分析物面板最具前景。有效的后 COVID 研究需要标准化病例定义、跨平台验证以及整合凝血检测和细胞外囊泡分析以提升组织信号检测。Cruz‐Altamirano,E 等 (20) 对先前 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染后登革热免疫失调进行试点蛋白质组学分析,得出先前 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 暴露可能通过交叉反应抗体增加登革热严重程度,促使 免疫应答 向 Th2 偏移并增强病毒复制。进一步,Parra‐González M. (21) 及其同事回顾了登革热与 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 的相互作用及其对临床结局的影响,发现共感染可能加重炎症、增加血管和器官损伤并使 治疗 复杂化。然而,抗体依赖增强 (ADE) 的确凿证据仍不充分,强调需进一步机制研究。Zhang,X. 对住院 HIV 与 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 共感染患者的蛋白质组学特征进行研究,结果显示 新型冠状病毒感染 在 HIV 患者中导致免疫调节、血栓形成和病毒进入通路紊乱。但仍需更大规模试验以确定共感染对 免疫应答 的影响。Mallapu G 等分析了 新型冠状病毒感染 幸存者有无败血症的程序性细胞死亡标志物,发现两种与疾病严重程度相关的分子特征。第一种特征表现为分泌型程序性细胞死亡标志物(IL‐1‐β、IFN‐γ、MHC I‐A、MHC II‐DRB1)水平升高,见于 新型冠状病毒感染‐败血症和非败血症 队列研究 患者。第二种特征包含细胞内程序性细胞死亡标志物(caspase‐1、caspase‐3、MLKL、p62/SQSTM1),特异于 新型冠状病毒感染‐败血症 队列研究。这些特征可作为疾病严重程度的生物标志物并指导危重症治疗。Calvo‐Silveira,S 等分析了 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染与肺炎链球菌定植及疾病严重程度的关系,发现共感染患者合并症更多、临床表现更重。有趣的是,非药物措施可能扰乱 S. pneumoniae 动态,COVID 疫苗接种 能防止共感染并降低疾病严重性。Currey J 等 (25) 使用 C57BL/6 小鼠模型研究流感与 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 的后病毒后遗症。他们以亚致死剂量的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 (MA30) 或流感 A (PR8) 感染小鼠,并在感染后第 14、21、28 天对肺和脑组织进行组织学分析和散装 RNA 测序,成功建立了 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 与流感感染后长期病理的组织特异性轨迹,为解析后病毒肺脑疾病机制提供了基础。该专题汇集了一系列重要手稿,涵盖 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染、疫苗 评估及共感染的多个关键方面,使读者能够全面了解这一复杂现象。值得注意的是,文中提出了多种关于疾病严重程度风险分析、病毒对 免疫应答 的评估以及 疫苗接种 效应的合理方案。此外,还识别出可能对未来研究有益的治疗靶点,包括与 长新冠 相关的目标。尽管疫情已超过六年,但仍有若干未解问题,尤其是感染后后遗症。因此,进一步研究对于阐明感染与共感染的复杂因素仍势在必行。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染和长新冠如何影响病毒共感染的 发病率,强调需要了解这些情况与其他病原体之间的相互作用。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究分析了住院 Omicron 患者的 T 细胞和 TCR 数据,重点关注 免疫应答 对 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 及其变体的影响,包括参与病毒复制和免疫逃逸的非结构蛋白。
analysis_zh.main_results: 相当比例的 TCR 针对 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 基因组 的表位,包括非结构蛋白;分析提示炎症小体活性下降和单核细胞分化受损,表明可能存在免疫耗竭或未成熟。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果凸显了 T 细胞保护性免疫、病毒复制周期和 HLA 类型之间的复杂关系,这些因素共同影响 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染中的 TCR 亲和力和克隆型形成。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果表明,理解 T 细胞应答及其受病毒因素和 HLA 类型调控的机制,可为改进 免疫应答 并管理 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染的长期影响提供策略指导。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究局限于住院 Omicron 患者,且缺乏长期随访数据,可能影响结果的普适性。鉴于这些限制,证据强度为中等。

title: Heritable transgenic schistosomes as a living platform for SARS-CoV-2 neutralizing antibody secretion.
abstract: We report the generation and propagation of not only the first heritable transgenic schistosome line but also a line that secretes a functional therapeutic protein in vivo. Using multiplexed CRISPR/Cas-mediated homology-directed knock-in targeted to a predicted genomic safe-harbor, we inserted a VHH–IgG1 Fc (termed C5-Fc) transgene into Schistosoma mansoni eggs. Single-miracidium infections of Biomphalaria glabrata yielded parental P0 lines; serial passage through snail and mouse hosts produced an F2 cohort in which all parasites carried the C5-Fc transgene and secreted C5-Fc into the murine venous circulation. Molecular assays confirmed chromosomal insertion, germline transmission and systemic secretion. Sera from mice harboring C5-Fc transgenic worms neutralized SARS-CoV-2 in vitro with potent activity consistent with the expected ACE2-binding blockade by the C5 variable domain of heavy-chain-only antibody (VHH). These results demonstrate (i) stable, heritable transgenesis of a platyhelminth, (ii) delivery of a biologically active antibody fragment by a live helminth in a mammalian host, and (iii) feasibility of using transgenic schistosomes as sustained, single-dose protein delivery platforms. This technology and delivery system enable new experimental approaches for schistosome biology and motivate exploration of living-foundry therapeutics. A heritable CRISPR knock-in in Schistosoma mansonigenerated a transgenic line that secreted a functional anti–SARS-CoV-2 antibody into mouse circulation. Virus neutralization by infected mouse sera demonstrated a worm-based living biofoundry for sustained, in vivo biologic delivery.

analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved generating and propagating a heritable transgenic schistosome line that secretes a functional therapeutic protein, using single-miracidium infections of Biomphalaria glabrata and serial passage through snail and mouse hosts to produce an F2 cohort.
analysis.methods: A multiplexed CRISPR/Cas-mediated homology-directed knock-in was used to insert a VHH–IgG1 Fc transgene into Schistosoma mansoni eggs, and molecular assays confirmed chromosomal insertion, germline transmission and systemic secretion.
analysis.main_results: Molecular assays confirmed chromosomal insertion, germline transmission and systemic secretion of the C5-Fc transgene, and sera from mice harboring C5-Fc transgenic worms neutralized SARS-CoV-2 in vitro with potent activity.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate the feasibility of using transgenic schistosomes as sustained, single-dose protein delivery platforms for therapeutic applications, including SARS-CoV-2 neutralizing antibodies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results suggest a potential new strategy for sustained in vivo delivery of biologically active antibodies, which could have implications for the development of novel therapeutic approaches against SARS-CoV-2 and related viruses.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to abstract-only evidence, and the results are based on in vitro neutralization assays, which may not fully reflect in vivo efficacy or long-term stability of the transgenic platform.

analysis.summary_en: This study presents a novel approach to delivering therapeutic proteins, specifically SARS-CoV-2 neutralizing antibodies, using transgenic schistosomes as a living platform. Researchers generated a heritable transgenic line of Schistosoma mansoni that secretes a functional antibody fragment into the murine venous circulation. Molecular assays confirmed chromosomal insertion, germline transmission, and systemic secretion of the transgene. Sera from mice with these transgenic worms neutralized SARS-CoV-2 in vitro, demonstrating the feasibility of using transgenic schistosomes for sustained, single-dose protein delivery. The findings suggest potential applications in developing new therapeutic strategies against SARS-CoV-2. However, the study is based on abstract-only evidence and relies on in vitro results, which may not fully capture in vivo efficacy or long-term stability. The results highlight the possibility of using live helminths as biologic delivery systems, opening new avenues for research and therapeutic development.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在开发一种新型递送治疗蛋白(特指严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2中和抗体)的方法,利用转基因血吸虫作为活体平台。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 研究通过单毛蚴感染双脐螺并经螺类与小鼠宿主连续传代,生成并传代携带可遗传转基因的血吸虫株系,最终获得F2 队列研究。
elements_zh.methods: 研究采用多重CRISPR/Cas介导的同源定向整合技术,将VHH–IgG1 Fc转基因插入曼氏血吸虫卵;分子检测确认染色体插入、生殖系传播及系统性分泌。
elements_zh.main_results: 分子检测确认C5-Fc转基因的染色体插入、生殖系传播及系统性分泌;携带C5-Fc转基因蠕虫的小鼠血清在体外以强效活性中和严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2,其活性与预期的ACE2结合阻断一致。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果证明转基因血吸虫可作为持续单次剂量蛋白递送平台用于治疗应用(包括严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2中和抗体),展现了该技术的可行性与创新性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果提示了一种潜在的新策略,用于持续体内递送生物活性抗体,可能对开发针对严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2及相关病毒的新型治疗方法产生影响。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 研究仅基于摘要证据,结果依赖体外中和实验,可能无法完全反映体内疗效或转基因平台的长期稳定性。

abstract_zh: 本研究报道了首个可遗传转基因血吸虫株系的生成与传代,以及体内分泌功能性治疗蛋白的株系。研究通过多重CRISPR/Cas介导的同源定向整合技术,将靶向预测基因组安全港的VHH–IgG1 Fc(命名为C5-Fc)转基因插入曼氏血吸虫卵。单毛蚴感染双脐螺后获得亲代P0株系;通过螺类与小鼠宿主的连续传代,获得F2 队列研究,其中所有寄生虫均携带C5-Fc转基因并将C5-Fc分泌至小鼠静脉循环。分子检测确认染色体插入、生殖系传播及系统性分泌。携带C5-Fc转基因蠕虫的小鼠血清在体外中和严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2,其活性与预期的ACE2结合阻断(由重链单域抗体C5可变区介导)一致。研究结果证明:(1)扁形动物稳定可遗传转基因,(2)活体蠕虫在哺乳动物宿主中递送生物活性抗体片段,(3)转基因血吸虫作为持续单次剂量蛋白递送平台的可行性。该技术与递送系统为血吸虫生物学研究提供新的实验方法,并为活体生物制药探索提供动力。曼氏血吸虫的可遗传CRISPR整合产生了一个分泌功能性抗严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2抗体进入小鼠循环的转基因株系。感染小鼠血清的病毒中和实验证明了基于蠕虫的活体生物工厂,可实现持续体内生物制剂递送。

media_mentions.content_title: Heritable transgenic schistosomes as a living platform for SARS-CoV-2 neutralizing antibody secretion - Nature Communications
media_mentions.content: Abstract We report the generation and propagation of not only the first heritable transgenic schistosome line but also a line that secretes a functional therapeutic protein in vivo. Using multiplexed CRISPR/Cas-mediated homology-directed knock-in targeted to a predicted genomic safe-harbor, we inserted a VHH–IgG1 Fc (termed C5-Fc) transgene into Schistosoma mansoni eggs. Single-miracidium infections of Biomphalaria glabrata yielded parental P0 lines; serial passage through snail and mouse hosts produced an F2 cohort in which all parasites carried the C5-Fc transgene and secreted C5-Fc into the murine venous circulation. Molecular assays confirmed chromosomal insertion, germline transmission and systemic secretion. Sera from mice harboring C5-Fc transgenic worms neutralized SARS-CoV-2 in vitro with potent activity consistent with the expected ACE2-binding blockade by the C5 variable domain of heavy-chain-only antibody (VHH). These results demonstrate (i) stable, heritable transgenesis of a platyhelminth, (ii) delivery of a biologically active antibody fragment by a live helminth in a mammalian host, and (iii) feasibility of using transgenic schistosomes as sustained, single-dose protein delivery platforms. This technology and delivery system enable new experimental approaches for schistosome biology and motivate exploration of living-foundry therapeutics. Similar content being viewed by others Introduction To date, heritably transgenic lines of schistosomes, or of any parasitic platyhelminth – clade Neodermata within phylum Platyhelminthes, have not been described. If such lines were available, progress in deciphering the biology and pathophysiology of these major neglected tropical disease (NTD) pathogens would be hastened, for example on fundamental questions such as what controls host range and specificity of the schistosome species, how do schistosomes locate their predilection site within the human host, which factors are decisive for bidirectional female-male interaction, and which genes encode target proteins of therapeutic value. As with other species, the ability to manipulate the schistosome would represent a step-change for the field and enable deep investigation of the (patho)biological nature of this pathogen. Transgenic lines of schistosomes also would be useful for investigating the value of helminth therapy for autoimmune and metabolic diseases1,2,3. The recent development of human challenge models of single-sex schistosome infections4,5 paves the way for clinical assessment of transgenic schistosomes as living foundries for synthetic biology applications6. Pertinent also are recent reports that exposure to lung-migrating helminths, including schistosomes, protect against Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection through macrophage-dependent T cell activation and remodeling of the lung environment7,8. Tractable, routine derivation of transgenic lines of schistosomes, and indeed other helminths that are used therapeutically in human challenge models9, would be unarguably welcome. Deploying Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats/CRISPR-associated (proteins) (CRISPR/Cas)-driven functional genomics including programmed knock out (KO) and knock-in (KI) mutagenesis for schistosomes was first reported in 2019, in research from our laboratory10. However, heritable transgenesis via insertion of a transgene into the germ line had not been achieved, reflecting multiple obstacles: a complex life cycle that cannot be completed in vitro, difficulties with transfection in a multicellular organism, limited germ-line access, lack of chromosomal safe-harbor sites, diploidy and dioecy, and sparse knowledge of secretion. We now report this advance, enabled by a combined suite of technical and conceptual innovations: 1) targeting transgene insertion to a predicted genome safe harbor site11,12; 2) deploying several overlapping guide RNAs to enhance the likelihood of RNA-guided chromosomal double stranded break (DSB) and homology directed repair (HDR) by transgene insertion13,14,15; and 3) by transfecting the immature egg stage of the schistosome16. Our goal was vertical transgene transmission via natural infection of the snail by the (transgenic) miracidium larval stage, and propagation of the transgenic schistosome line. Derivation of a heritably transgenic line of S. mansoni represents transformative progress in tropical medicine. The line was established using CRISPR-based knock-in of an antibody-encoding transgene into the genome of the egg stage of S. mansoni. A parental female P0 and a parental male P0 generation were established by single miracidium exposure of the intermediate host, the aquatic gastropod Biomphalaria glabrata. Mice were infected with these P0 generation female and male line cercariae. Eggs subsequently recovered from the mice represented the F1 generation of the transgenic line, which we termed the “C5-Fc line”. In turn, snails were infected with miracidia hatched from the eggs. In this way, the C5-Fc line was propagated through to the F2 generation (Fig. 1). The transgene encodes an IgG1 Fc-fusion of C5, a variable domain of heavy-chain-only antibody (VHH)17, which targets the angiotensin converting enzyme 2 (ACE2) receptor binding site of the spike protein of SARS-CoV-218. The C5-Fc line of schistosomes secreted the VHH into the blood of mice infected with these worms, and sera from these mice potently neutralized the SARS-CoV-2 virion. Results Virus neutralization by recombinant camelid antibodies Amino acid sequences of three VHHs targeting the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein were obtained from the literature – VHH-C518 and VHH-E and VHH-V19 along with a variant of VHH-C5 that was fused to the human IgG1 Fc domain, which we termed VHH-C5-Fc (Supplementary Fig. 1). All four VHHs expressed at high concentrations in HEK293F cells and were isolated in recombinant forms to >95% purity with single step, immobilized metal ion affinity chromatography (IMAC) (Supplementary Fig. 2a). Recombinant VHHs were assayed for virus neutralizing capacity using two independent assays: 1) an immunofluorescence-visualized pseudotyped lentiviral plaque assay20, and 2) by the SARS-CoV-2 plaque reduction neutralization test (PRNT)21. For the pseudotyped lentiviral plaque assay, neutralization was benchmarked against the Human SARS-CoV-2 Convalescent Serology Standard from the National Institute for Biological Standards and Control (NIBSC), NIBSC 20/13022. All VHHs neutralized pseudotyped lentivirus in the low microgram (VHH-E, VHH-V) to nanogram per milliliter ranges (VHH-C5, VHH-C5-Fc) VHH-C5-Fc was more potent than VHH-C5 with IC50 values of 5 ng/ml and 273 ng/ml, respectively (Supplementary Fig. 2b). After confirming the neutralizing activity of the VHHs against pseudotyped lentivirus (an assay surrogate for SARS-CoV-2), we tested their neutralizing capacity directly against an isolate, SARS-CoV-2 USA-WA1/202023, by the PRNT21. Neutralization of SARS-CoV-2 in this assay was benchmarked against the Human SARS-CoV-2 Serology Standard from the Frederick National Laboratory for Cancer Research (https://frederick.cancer.gov/resources/universal-standards-reference-materials/human-sars-cov-2-serology-standard)22,24; referred to here as FNLCR serum. Dose-dependent neutralization was obtained with all VHHs (Fig. 2a) and as also seen in the pseudotyped lentivirus assay, VHH-C5 and VHH-C5-Fc were the more potent of these VHHs, with IC50 values of 791 ng/ml and 24 ng/ml, respectively (Fig. 2b). Based on the IC50 values for HEK293F-expressed VHHs for neutralization of SARS-CoV-2, we selected the VHH-IgG1 Fc fusion, C5-Fc, as the transgene to insert into the configurable expression chassis for RNA-programmed CRISPR/Cas9 delivery into the germline of S. mansoni. Figure 3 diagrammatically depicts the transgene, its components and expression product, the CRISPR knock-in strategy, including orientation of the promoter, signal peptide, C5-Fc coding region and amino acid sequence, dimerization of the VHH endowed by the IgG1 Fc fusion partner, and terminator motif (Fig. 3a–d), along with potential knock out as well as knock in alleles following transfection of the schistosome egg with the donor transgene and RNPs (Fig. 3e, f). Supplementary Fig. 3 provides the donor transgene sequence, while Supplementary Table 1 lists the nucleotide sequences of the guide RNAs and oligonucleotide primers deployed in the study. Transgene construct encoding the C5-Fc anti-SARS-CoV-2 antibody For insertion into the S. mansoni genome, we targeted a site in Genome Safe Harbor 1 (GSH1) on chromosome 3 of S. mansoni12 and deployed three overlapping guide RNAs for programmed CRISPR/Cas9 knock-in, a target site and tactics that we had previously shown to be both not apparently harmful to the targeted schistosome egg and effective for insertion of a reporter gene into S. mansoni genome12. To prepare a synthetic transgene construct encoding the C5-Fc anti-SARS-CoV-2 antibody, we included short (50 nt each) left and right side homology arms, and the promoter and terminator of an endogenous ubiquitin gene of S. mansoni, Gene ID, Smp_335990, UBB protein (WormBase Parasite, version WBPS19)25,26,27 to drive expression of the transgene (Fig. 3a, b). The rationale for using this promoter was that using an endogenous, ubiquitously expressed gene promoter (like ubiquitin) has advantages, especially in non-model organisms28,29, including broad, constitutive expression in tissues, cells and developmental stages30. Indeed, based on transcriptomics data for this schistosome, the Smp_335990 gene is strongly, ubiquitously, and stage-independently expressed31,32. We anticipated its compatibility with native transcription machinery since an endogenous promoter would be likely to be recognized and accurately regulated by the helminth’s own transcription machinery (transcription factors, chromatin context) and this could be expected to reduce the risk of failure or silencing. Non-endogenous – viral or foreign – promoters can trigger epigenetic silencing, especially over time or in specific tissues33. The promoter and terminator sequences of Smp_335990 represent tractable and not overly large regulatory elements for donor constructs12,26 and, indeed, we had previously used the ubiquitin promoter and its terminator in transgene constructs for knock-in experiments, with Cas9 and Cas12a, encoding a GFP reporter, inserted at the same GSH1 site26. The secretory signal peptide from the hookworm protein, ASP2, known to actively drive secretion of diverse helminth proteins in mammalian cell lines34, served to direct the nanobody fusion protein into the schistosome’s secretory pathway. Translation initiation is a major rate limiting step in protein synthesis and given the positive impact of translation of the amino acids encoded by codons 3 to 535, we preemptively inserted two extra residues, Lys-Leu, at amino acid positions 3 and 4 of the signal peptide, MVKLVLVPLLALLAVSVH, aiming to improve protein synthesis of the transgene-encoded nanobody and, in turn, secretion of the recombinant C5-Fc fusion protein (Fig. 3c, d). Our experimental approach had two strategic components. First, using S. mansoni as a biological foundry exploited the male schistosome’s long-term survival to enable continuous in situ production of the therapeutic transgene product. Second, fusing the C5 VHH to the Fc region of human IgG1 induced dimerization, yielding a bivalent antibody with two identical antigen-binding sites to enhance SARS-CoV-2 neutralization (Fig. 3d). We leveraged Fc-induced bivalency to amplify the potency of the parental VHH through the avidity effect. – a key advantage for targeting viruses with repeating surface antigens like the SARS-CoV-236. Indeed, recombinant C5-Fc expressed in HEK293F cells was >30-fold more potent than C5 alone in the same system (Fig. 2). Additionally, the Fc domain promotes neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn)-mediated recycling, extending serum half-life and improving tissue distribution37. Finally, the Fc domain confers effector functions, including antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and phagocytosis that could aid in the detection and clearance of virus-infected cells38,39. Derivation of the C5-Fc line and propagation through intermediate snail and definitive mammalian hosts Figure 4a schematically displays the technical steps used to derive the C5-Fc line of transgenic S. mansoni. In vitro laid (immature) schistosome eggs (IVLEs) were transfected by electroporation with three overlapping RNPs targeting GSH1 on chromosome 3 of S. mansoni12 along with a 5′-modified-double stranded DNA donor encoding C5-Fc. A polymerase chain reaction (PCR)-based screen using transgene specific primers of a sample of the hatching population of these eggs and miracidia confirmed the presence of the C5-Fc transgene (302 bp amplicon; Figs. 4b, c and 4004 bp amplicon; Supplementary Fig. 4e). Forty-eight Biomphalaria glabrata snails were each exposed to a single miracidium hatched from this cohort (monomiracidial infection40). By 12 weeks later, C5-Fc-positive cercariae had been shed from three of the 48 snails (6.3%), whereas 16 snails shed wild type cercariae. Male cercariae shed from one of those three transgene positive snails, female cercariae from a second, and the third died before yielding enough cercariae for mouse infections (Supplementary Fig. 4b). The sex of cercariae shed from each snail was determined using a competitive PCR41; a 404 bp amplicon specific for the rpS4 gene, located only on the Z chromosome – confirming the sex of the cercariae as male, and a 195 bp amplicon of W6 repetitive element for the W chromosome, confirming the sex of the cercariae as female. In this PCR, a higher Z-specific gene: a W-localized repetitive element copy ratio results in the presence of both 404 and 195 bp amplicons and indicates male DNA, whereas the presence of only the 195 bp amplicon indicates female DNA. Figure 4b shows representative PCR results including the demonstration of both P0 transgenic and WT cercariae from the monomiracidial infection of the snails. Each of six mice was exposed first to ~90 male cercariae and then a few weeks later (when the female cercariae became available) to ~100 female transgene (TG)-positive cercariae, aiming to establish a sexually reproducing population of P0 generation transgenic schistosomes within each mouse. About eight weeks after the infection with the female cercariae, the mice were euthanized, and adult schistosomes perfused from the portal circulation. Among the perfused worms, we observed up to five paired adult schistosomes among the ~20 worms obtained from each mouse. These adult schistosomes represented the foundation P0 generation of the C5-Fc line. Concurrently, we also recovered the schistosome eggs from the livers of the mice, the eggs representing the F1 generation. Samples of the adult P0 female and male worms were positive for the C5-Fc transgene (Fig. 4b) as were samples of the F1 generation eggs (Supplemental Fig. 4. b-e). Eggs of this F1 cohort, isolated under aseptic conditions by collagenase digestion of all six mouse livers42, pooled into a single digest, were induced to hatch. Again, 48 snails were individually exposed to miracidia hatched from this transgene positive cohort of F1 generation eggs. In turn, shedding of cercariae was periodically induced from the snails from five weeks after exposure. By 12 weeks, C5-Fc-positive cercariae had been shed from seven of the 48 snails (14.6%); five of these snails shed female cercariae and two shed male cercariae. Over several weeks from the first appearance of transgenic F1 generation cercariae onwards, and as sufficient numbers of cercariae became available, six mice were each infected with ~100 female and ~100 male cercariae of the F1 generation of the nascent C5-Fc line. In turn, eggs were recovered from the livers of these mice, which also were C5-Fc positive, and thus represented the F2 generation. The F2 generation was similarly propagated, with miracidia hatched from F2 eggs. PCR of F2 cercariae from individual snails infected by these F2 generation miracidia showed a 97% transgenic rate – 33 of 34 snails shed transgenic F2 cercariae (Fig. 4c, lower gel). Figure 4c (upper gel) shows PCR screening of a representative batch of cercariae from nine of these 33 snails; four snails produced male and five produced female cercariae (Fig. 4c, lower gel). Amplicons of Z and/or W chromosome- localized markers provided a DNA integrity control. C5-Fc secreted by TG schistosomes potently neutralizes SARS-CoV-2 in vitro C5‐Fc produced by transgenic S. mansoni was detected in both excretory/secretory products (ESP) and sera of infected mice and mediated potent neutralization of the SARS‐CoV‐2 virus. Figure 5a provides a schematic overview of our assessment approach. Specifically, a quantitative capture ELISA revealed the presence of C5-Fc in ESP from pools of adult, mixed sex schistosomes, confirming secretion of C5‐Fc by the schistosomes at a concentration of 54.9 ± 4 ng/ml culture medium (Fig. 5b). The ELISA detected much lower C5‐Fc levels in the ESP of two negative-control worm groups: worms transfected with donor transgene but without RNPs, or mock‐transfected worms (Fig. 5b). Thereafter, we examined whether ESP containing the secreted C5-Fc could neutralize SARS-CoV-2 virus, as described for C5-Fc in the original report for recombinant C5-Fc18. We assessed neutralization of SARS-CoV-2 virus using the PRNT assay, in which the FNLCR was included as the positive control (Fig. 5c, d). ESP and FNLCR were diluted up to 31,250-fold, and neutralization levels plotted alongside the negative control ESP groups. ESP from the transgenic schistosomes diluted 1/108 completely ( ~ 100%) neutralized SARS-CoV-2, with an IC50 of 1,443 dilution factor (DF), a neutralization capacity only modestly lower…

title: Hyperglycemia in Cats Infected by SARS-CoV-2: Pancreatic Alterations and Potential Antiviral Therapeutics
abstract: Cats represent a susceptible host and a possible translational model for investigating coronavirus pathogenesis and therapeutics. Recent immunohistochemical (IHC) and histopathological studies in both human and feline tissues have demonstrated SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein (NP) and spike protein expression within pancreatic islet cells, following a classic temporal infection course. Notably, IHC analysis also reveals NP expression within exocrine ductal epithelial cells. Given that ductal epithelium functions as an islet progenitor pool during tissue injury or metabolic stress, pancreotropic coronaviruses may gain access to the endocrine compartment by exploiting this intrinsic cellular differentiation pathway. Although the precise mechanisms governing intra-islet viral entry remain to be elucidated, this review highlights the capacity of SARS-CoV-2 to compromise both the exocrine (digestive) and endocrine functions of the pancreas. Finally, we evaluate the therapeutic potential of direct-acting antivirals—specifically RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) and protease inhibitors—as monotherapies and in synergistic combination to limit pancreatic injury and mitigate the diabetogenic effects of coronaviruses across both acute infection and post-acute sequelae, such as human long-COVID syndrome.

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on SARS-CoV-2 and its impact on the pancreas in cats, exploring the pathogenesis and potential antiviral therapeutics related to pancreatic alterations and diabetogenic effects.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review synthesizes recent immunohistochemical (IHC) and histopathological studies in human and feline tissues, highlighting SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein (NP) and spike protein expression within pancreatic islet cells and exocrine ductal epithelial cells. These findings are based on a classic temporal infection course observed in both species.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that SARS-CoV-2 can compromise both the exocrine and endocrine functions of the pancreas, with evidence of viral protein expression in islet cells and ductal epithelial cells. It also emphasizes the potential of direct-acting antivirals, such as RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) and protease inhibitors, to mitigate pancreatic injury and diabetogenic effects.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The precise mechanisms of intra-islet viral entry remain unclear, indicating a gap in understanding. Additionally, the review notes that while antiviral therapeutics are evaluated, their efficacy in mitigating long-term pancreatic effects is not fully established.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests prioritizing research into the mechanisms of SARS-CoV-2-induced pancreatic injury and the development of antiviral therapies targeting both acute and post-acute sequelae, such as long-COVID syndrome, in feline models.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the effects of SARS-CoV-2 on the pancreas in cats, highlighting the presence of viral proteins in both islet cells and exocrine ductal epithelial cells. It discusses the potential of antiviral therapies, including RdRp and protease inhibitors, to reduce pancreatic damage and diabetogenic effects. However, the exact mechanisms of viral entry into islet cells are not yet fully understood, and further research is needed to address these gaps. The findings suggest that feline models may provide valuable insights into the pathogenesis and treatment of SARS-CoV-2-related pancreatic complications in humans, particularly in the context of long-COVID syndrome.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述聚焦于严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2对猫胰腺的影响,探讨其发病机制及与胰腺改变和糖尿病发生风险相关的潜在抗病毒药物治疗策略。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本综述综合了近期人类和猫组织中的免疫组织化学(IHC)及组织病理学研究,强调了严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2核衣壳蛋白(NP)及刺突蛋白在胰腺岛细胞和外分泌导管上皮细胞中的表达。这些发现基于在两种物种中观察到的经典时间感染进程。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 综述得出结论:严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2可损害胰腺的外分泌和内分泌功能,并有证据表明病毒蛋白在岛细胞和导管上皮细胞中表达。同时强调了直接作用型抗病毒药物(如RNA依赖性RNA聚合酶抑制剂和蛋白酶抑制剂)在减轻胰腺损伤和糖尿病发生风险方面的潜力。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 胰岛内病毒进入的精确机制仍不清楚,表明在理解上存在缺口。此外,综述指出,尽管已评估抗病毒药物治疗策略,但其在缓解长期胰腺影响方面的有效性尚未完全确立。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 综述建议优先研究严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2诱导胰腺损伤的机制,并开发针对急性期与后急性期并发症(如长新冠综合征)的抗病毒药物治疗策略,在猫模型中进行验证。

abstract_zh: 猫是一种易感宿主,并可能作为研究冠状病毒发病机制及其治疗策略的转化模型。近期在人类和猫组织中的免疫组织化学(IHC)及组织病理学研究显示,在经典时间感染进程后,严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2核衣壳蛋白(NP)及刺突蛋白在胰腺岛细胞中表达。值得注意的是,IHC分析还在外分泌导管上皮细胞中检测到NP表达。由于导管上皮在组织损伤或代谢应激期间可作为胰岛祖细胞库,嗜胰腺冠状病毒可能通过利用这种内在细胞分化途径进入内分泌区室。尽管尚未阐明调控胰岛内病毒进入的精确机制,但本综述强调了严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2损害胰腺外分泌(消化)和内分泌功能的能力。最后,我们评估了直接作用型抗病毒药物——特别是RNA依赖性RNA聚合酶(RdRp)抑制剂和蛋白酶抑制剂——作为单药治疗及协同联合疗法,以限制胰腺损伤并减轻冠状病毒感染急性期与后急性期并发症(如人类长新冠综合征)的糖尿病发生风险。

title: SARS-CoV-2 ORF8: an accessory protein at the interface of immune evasion and inflammation
abstract: SARS-CoV-2 ORF8 is a rapidly evolving accessory protein that modulates host immunity through both intracellular and extracellular mechanisms. Intracellularly, ORF8 disrupts antigen presentation by reducing cell-surface MHC-I and is linked to endoplasmic reticulum remodeling and altered stress responses. Extracellularly, secreted ORF8 behaves as a virokine that can amplify inflammatory programs in myeloid and dendritic cells, with potential implications for acute severity and tissue-specific pathology. ORF8 is also reported to antagonize type I interferon induction through effects on IRF3-dependent pathways. Clinically, circulating ORF8 has been associated with disease severity, and persistent detection of ORF8 after viral RNA becomes undetectable has been reported in some individuals with post-acute symptoms. However, whether this persistence reflects a direct pathogenic role or instead marks ongoing viral burden and immune activation remains unresolved. In this review, we summarize recent findings on the pleiotropic effects of ORF8 and outline key priorities to clarify when ORF8 acts primarily as an immune-evasion factor, an inflammatory amplifier, or both. Collectively, the evidence reviewed here identifies ORF8 as a promising candidate for further mechanistic studies, whose biomarker potential and therapeutic relevance warrant rigorous evaluation in acute and post-acute COVID-19.

analysis.summary_en: This review focuses on SARS-CoV-2 ORF8, an accessory protein with dual roles in immune evasion and inflammation. ORF8 modulates host immunity through intracellular mechanisms, such as disrupting antigen presentation by reducing MHC-I expression and altering endoplasmic reticulum function. Extracellularly, it acts as a virokine that amplifies inflammatory responses in myeloid and dendritic cells, potentially contributing to disease severity. ORF8 also antagonizes type I interferon induction via IRF3-dependent pathways. Clinically, its persistence in some individuals with post-acute symptoms is linked to disease severity, though its pathogenic role remains unresolved. The review highlights the need for further mechanistic studies to determine whether ORF8 functions primarily as an immune-evasion factor, an inflammatory amplifier, or both, emphasizing its potential as a biomarker and therapeutic target in acute and post-acute COVID-19.

title: Divergent lipid utilization strategies of SARS-CoV-2 and MERS-CoV revealed by comparative multi-omics profiling of infected mouse lung tissues
abstract: Background Coronaviruses (CoVs), including severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) and Middle East respiratory syndrome (MERS-CoV), cause respiratory infections with distinct clinical outcomes and case fatality rates. However, the molecular basis of these differences remains unclear. In this study, we sought to define virus-specific host metabolic programs by directly comparing multiomics profiles of the lungs of lethally infected mouse models. Methods We performed integrated multiomics analyses, including untargeted metabolomics, transcriptomics, and targeted lipidomics, of lung tissues from human angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (hiACE2)-human dipeptidyl peptidase 4 (hDPP4) double-knock-in (DKI) mice infected in SARS-CoV-2 or MERS-CoV. Data Integration Analysis and Biomarker discovery using Latent cOmponents (DIABLO) was applied across all three omics layers to identify key distinguishing molecular patterns. Additionally, in vitro lipid droplet kinetics were examined in infected Vero E6 cells to validate temporal differences in lipid remodeling. Results We identified two distinct strategies for lipid utilization. SARS-CoV-2 infection showed strong activation of energy and amino acid metabolism at an early stage of infection (3 days post infection, DPI), whereas MERS-CoV infection was characterized by sustained alterations in lipid and nucleotide metabolism. Integrative DIABLO analysis of all three omics layers revealed that the key distinguishing features clustered into virus-specific molecular signatures: a triacylglycerol–lipid droplet–interferon axis for SARS-CoV-2 and a phospholipid–sphingolipid–membrane hub for MERS-CoV. In vitro lipid droplet kinetics in infected Vero E6 cells confirmed this temporal difference, with SARS-CoV-2 peaking earlier than MERS-CoV. Conclusion These findings show that β-CoVs exploit host lipid metabolism through virus-specific and time-dependent remodeling programs, providing a framework for understanding differential pathogenesis and developing host-directed antiviral strategies.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed why SARS-CoV-2 and MERS-CoV cause distinct clinical outcomes despite both being betacoronaviruses, noting that the molecular basis for these differences remains unclear.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The research used lethally infected mouse models with humanized receptors (hiACE2-hDPP4 double-knock-in mice) to compare multi-omics profiles of lung tissues infected with SARS-CoV-2 or MERS-CoV.
analysis.methods: Integrated multi-omics analyses included untargeted metabolomics, transcriptomics, and targeted lipidomics of lung tissues, with DIABLO applied across all three omics layers to identify key distinguishing molecular patterns. In vitro lipid droplet kinetics were examined in infected Vero E6 cells to validate temporal differences in lipid remodeling.
analysis.main_results: SARS-CoV-2 infection showed strong activation of energy and amino acid metabolism at 3 days post infection, whereas MERS-CoV infection was characterized by sustained alterations in lipid and nucleotide metabolism. Integrative DIABLO analysis revealed virus-specific molecular signatures: a triacylglycerol–lipid droplet–interferon axis for SARS-CoV-2 and a phospholipid–sphingolipid–membrane hub for MERS-CoV.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as evidence that β-coronaviruses exploit host lipid metabolism through virus-specific and time-dependent remodeling programs, providing a framework for understanding differential pathogenesis.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study suggests that targeting host lipid metabolism pathways could inform the development of host-directed antiviral strategies tailored to specific betacoronaviruses.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to mouse models and in vitro cell systems, which may not fully recapitulate human infection dynamics, and the study relies on abstract-level data without detailed quantitative or mechanistic validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study compared multi-omics profiles of lung tissues from humanized mouse models infected with SARS-CoV-2 or MERS-CoV to elucidate virus-specific host metabolic programs. SARS-CoV-2 infection triggered early activation of energy and amino acid metabolism, while MERS-CoV induced sustained lipid and nucleotide metabolism alterations. Integrative DIABLO analysis identified distinct molecular signatures: a triacylglycerol–lipid droplet–interferon axis for SARS-CoV-2 and a phospholipid–sphingolipid–membrane hub for MERS-CoV. In vitro lipid droplet kinetics confirmed earlier remodeling peaks for SARS-CoV-2. The findings suggest β-coronaviruses exploit host lipid metabolism through virus-specific and time-dependent programs, offering a framework for understanding differential pathogenesis and developing host-directed antiviral strategies.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究探讨了为什么严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2和MERS-CoV尽管都是β冠状病毒,却导致不同的临床结果,指出这些差异的分子基础仍不清楚。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究使用了具有人类化受体(hiACE2-hDPP4双敲入小鼠)的致命性感染小鼠模型,以比较严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2或MERS-CoV感染肺组织的多组学特征。
elements_zh.methods: 整合的多组学分析包括对肺组织进行非靶向代谢组学、转录组学和靶向脂质组学,并通过DIABLO在三个组学层面应用,以识别关键的区分性分子模式。为验证脂质重塑的时间差异,还检测了感染Vero E6细胞中的脂滴动力学。
elements_zh.main_results: 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2感染在感染后3天表现出强烈的能量和氨基酸代谢激活,而MERS-CoV感染则以脂质和核苷酸代谢的持续改变为特征。整合DIABLO分析揭示了病毒特异性的分子特征:严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2具有三酰甘油-脂质滴-干扰素轴,而MERS-CoV则具有磷脂-鞘脂-膜枢纽。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为β冠状病毒通过病毒特异性和时间依赖性的脂质重塑程序利用宿主脂质代谢,为理解差异性发病机制提供了框架。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 本研究表明,针对宿主脂质代谢通路可能有助于开发特定针对β冠状病毒的抗病毒药物策略。
